cards.title: Hopping chain: T = Q_AB^+ Q_AC satisfies the A-C intertwining conditions (Tcond) for (L_A,L_B,L_C) = (4,8,2), (4,12,2), (4,16,2)
cards.statement: On the half-filled hopping chain (Q_ij = sin(pi(i-j)/2)/(pi(i-j))) with (L_A,L_B,L_C) = (4,8,2), (4,12,2), (4,16,2), the Moore-Penrose choice T := Q_AB^+ Q_AC satisfies Q_AB T = Q_AC to residual 3.6e-17, 1.8e-17, 1.8e-17 (round-off; the tex quotes 1.4e-17, 7.0e-17, 2.3e-17), ||T|| = 0.5524, 0.3779, 0.2894 < 1 (so T*T <= 1), and T* Q_BB T <= Q_CC <= 1 - T*(1 - Q_BB) T with both margins (smallest eigenvalues) 0.1216, 0.1510, 0.1630 (tex: 0.552, 0.378, 0.289 and 0.122, 0.151, 0.163), as computed by numerics/kb-checks-2026-09-23/tcond_check.py (numpy pinv; REF-DEP-CFT-A1's reproduction). Numerical; no continuum or general-geometry statement: at (6,12,3) and (8,16,4) the same T violates (Tcond) (margins -0.133 and -0.464, ||T|| = 0.80 and 1.29; tcond_check_extra.out). The repository's numerics/optimality/lower_bound.py does not compute this T: it optimises (T, Z_c) by Powell from T = 0, and lb.log prints ||T|| = 0.5503, 0.3776, 0.2851 of that optimised T and no residual.

cards.title: A-C restriction bound: (Tcond) implies E_AC = 0 exactly; applied on the hopping chain (4,8,2), (4,12,2), (4,16,2)
cards.statement: Proved, as an implication (Prop. prop:AC-zero, rigor/optimality_second_order.tex:408-434): if some T: h_C -> h_B satisfies (eq:Tcond) Q_AB T = Q_AC, T*T <= 1, T* Q_BB T <= Q_CC <= 1 - T*(1 - Q_BB) T, then X* := (0 T) and Z := (1/2) 1_B (+) Q_CC give (X, Z) in F whose recovered symbol on h_A (+) h_C is the vacuum one, so a gauge-invariant quasi-free channel beta in C reproduces omega exactly on A(A) v A(C): E_AC = 0 and the restriction bound (eq:AC-bound) of Lemma lem:restriction gives nothing. Application: the hypothesis is established only numerically, on the half-filled hopping chain for (L_A,L_B,L_C) = (4,8,2), (4,12,2), (4,16,2), where T = Q_AB^+ Q_AC satisfies (Tcond) (card ac-intertwiner-exists-hopping-chain); on these three chains E_AC = 0 exactly, consistent with the direct convex minimisation of numerics/optimality/lower_bound.py (lb.log: E_AC = 1.53e-9, 9.83e-10, 6.99e-9, solver floor, against -log F(omega_AC, omega_A (x) omega_C) = 3.17e-3, 1.66e-3, 1.03e-3). Nothing is claimed for the continuum or for other geometries: lb.log's third row (6,12,3) gives E_AC = 2.27e-5 (E_AC/z^2 = 0.0045), and at (6,12,3) and (8,16,4) the Moore-Penrose T violates (Tcond) (margins -0.133, -0.464; numerics/kb-checks-2026-09-23/tcond_check_extra.out). The tex's conclusion that the O8 route ('bound the Bures distance of the vacuum A-C state to the B-mediated ones') yields no bound at all (:450-457) extrapolates from these three chains by a heuristic mechanism and is not part of this card.

cards.title: The all-channel second-order optimum equals the isometric-orbit value: kappa_opt = 1 - theta = 0.616 +- 0.003 (numerical; conditional on H1, H2, H3)
cards.statement: Phase 5 answer to 'the exact value of the all-channel optimum (non-isometric channels)'. Analytic (rigor/exact_optimum_tangent_problem.tex, refereed, repairs applied): every feasible quasi-free channel is exactly (co-isometry V, isometry loss N = 1 - XX* >= 0, noise 0 <= Y = Z - X Q_BB X* <= N); the leading-order problem is a convex tangent programme, and the isometric-orbit optimum (value (1 - theta) g_Q(deltadot)) is its global optimum iff (a) M_* = Herm((t_* Q)_DD) >= 0 and M_* - tau_* >= 0 (tau_* = (t_*)_DD, as forms) and (e) the one-sided endpoint functional E(zeta) = 2 b(delta_*, A(zeta,0,0)) >= 0 for every admissible (dissipative) isometry generator zeta. For the two model boundary directions, E(zeta_inf) = 2 lambda (1 - theta) g_Q > 0 is proved and E(zeta_0) > 0 is numerical; the reduction of the WHOLE cone of admissible generators to these two directions is proved only for vector fields (Prop 4.10) and is otherwise a declared hypothesis H3 (referee2_exact_optimum_tangent_problem.tex S1: multiplicity > 1 shift semigroups and unbounded skew-adjoint multiplication operators escape the argument). Numerical (F2, rigid parameter-free modular frame with exact Moebius rigidity): (a) holds in the limit (violation lambda_min/||M_*|| = -4.1e-3 ... -3.7e-4 at h = 0.24 ... 0.03, scaling as h^1.15 and 1/Ymax, achievable gain ~ h^1.85 -> 0); (e) on the model cone: E(zeta_inf) > 0 is proved; at zeta_0 the corner term (1/2) M_*(0,0)/h = +10.3, +16.1, +24.7, +37.2 at h = 0.24 ... 0.03 (~h^-0.60, the scheme-invariant continuum quantity; the discrete total +34 ... +258 is upwind-viscosity dominated and is not the margin) diverges, so A(zeta_0,0,0) is not in the form domain, E(zeta_0) = +infinity and (e) is VACUOUS at zeta_0 rather than satisfied with a margin (F1 Rem 4.11(ii), Prop 4.10(5)); no sign change in h, Y, Ymax. Hence, numerically and under H3, non-isometric quasi-free channels (isometry loss, noise, non-surjective isometries) do NOT lower the second-order recovery error: kappa_opt = 1 - theta with theta = 0.384 +- 0.003 (F3, two discretisations reconciled; S10's 0.300 was a taper-suppressed lower bound), i.e. E^(2) = (0.616 +- 0.003) f_2 z^2 per chirality. Conditional on H1 (differentiability along the scaled family), H2 (minimisers within the scaled-family form) and H3 (cone hypothesis) of the F1 document; the unconditional statements remain E_rec <= 0.616 f_2 z^2 (1+o(1)) (E1 upper half for isometric channels + theta) and E_rec >= dual form (optimality_all_channels.tex eq. (10)). Exact fidelity for NON-isometric channels was not needed: the optimum is attained on the isometric orbit, where E1 applies. Open: analytic proof of (a) and (e); H1, H2, H3; closed form of theta (Wiener-Hopf problem, prop:thetaframe); analytic proof that theta > 0 (E_D u E_D not self-adjoint).

cards.statement: For every normal unital CP even beta: A(BC) -> A(B), with xi_g = beta(a(g)) Omega, Kadison-Schwarz for a(g) and a*(g) gives Z >= Gram(xi) and 1 - Z >= Gram(S_B xi); projecting with Pi := P_- P_1 onto the one-particle charge -1 sector preserves these (the projections commute with Delta_B, Baumgaertel-Jurke-Lledo Cor. 5.4); D(S_B) on one-particle vectors is exactly the localised ones (BJL Prop. 5.3, closed graph Lemma 4.10). Hence the PROJECTED vector satisfies Pi xi_g = a(X* g) Omega with X* g in h_B (thm:range <1>1-<1>2), and (X, Z) in F with Q^beta = Q_rec(X, Z), Z = Q^beta_DD. The unprojected xi_g need not be a one-particle vector (only Pi xi_g is used), so xi_g = a(X* g) Omega itself is not claimed.

cards.title: The C^{1,1} extension of the zero-collar map is implementable on Fock space (uhlmann_upper_bound.tex Cor. 2.7, Prop. 3.1)
cards.statement: Geometry of rigor/uhlmann_upper_bound.tex (eq:geom, l. 72-74): A = (-infinity, 0), D = (0, 1), I = AD = (-infinity, 1), I' = (1, infinity), zeta = s (a = infinity, L = 1). Let k~_s be the flow of the vector field -chi d/dx, with chi = 0 on x <= 0 and chi(x) = x^2 beta(x-1) on x > 0 (def:ext). (k~_s) for s real is a one-parameter group of C^{1,1} increasing bijections of R, equal to the identity outside (0, 2). For s >= 0, moreover, k~_s(x) = x/(1+sx) = k_s(x) on [0, 1] (lem:ext (E1), (E2)); the document states (E1)-(E4) only for every s >= 0 (l. 122). (E2) does not extend to s < 0. At s = -1, x = 0.9, x/(1+sx) = 9 lies outside [0, 2], which k~_s maps onto itself. The flow value depends on beta, which the document fixes only by its properties (def:ext, l. 105-106): 1.756 for the standard smooth step, 1.629 for beta^2, 1.905 for beta = 1 on [0, 1/2] (refb6_flow.py). For every allowed beta, (E2) fails for all s <= -1/2; for -1/2 < s < 0 it depends on beta (with beta = 1 on [0, 1/2] it holds for -1/3 <= s < 0; with the standard step it fails for every s < 0). Let W~_s be the unitary push-forward of k~_s on half-densities. Then P_- W~_s P_+ is Hilbert-Schmidt for every s. prop:HS gives an explicit bound when ||id - k~_s||_inf <= 1/2 (l. 286-287). Every other s follows from W~_s = (W~_{s/n})^n, since products of unitaries with Hilbert-Schmidt off-diagonal parts have Hilbert-Schmidt off-diagonal parts. The other block is P_+ W~_s P_- = (P_- W~_{-s} P_+)^*, Hilbert-Schmidt by the same argument. The document omits that step, although its 'every 0 <= s <= 1' (l. 293) and cor:implementer's 'every s in R' use prop:HS beyond its hypothesis: with the standard step, ||id - k~_s||_inf = 0.61 at s = 0.5 and 0.95 at s = 1 (refb6_flow.py). So there is a unitary Gamma(W~_s) of Fock space, unique up to a phase, with Gamma(W~_s) a(f) Gamma(W~_s)^* = a(W~_s f) for all f (cor:implementer). The same holds for W~_s(1_{L^2(I)} (+) W'), with W' a unitary of L^2(I') such that P_-(1 (+) W')P_+ and P_+(1 (+) W')P_- are both Hilbert-Schmidt. The Shale-Stinespring criterion needs both off-diagonal blocks; an example is W' = e^{ish'} with h' self-adjoint, as in def:admissible, l. 745-754. The document's one-sided condition is not enough (DOCUMENT ERROR note). For s >= 0, Gamma(W~_s) X Gamma(W~_s)^* = beta_s(X) on the CAR generators of F(I), and Psi_s = Gamma(W~_s)^* Omega is a vector representative of the recovered state omega~_s = omega_{J_s} o beta_s on F(I) (prop:vector; (C4), l. 76-80). The Shale-Stinespring criterion (and Araki 1970) is cited, not obtained ('Screenshot: NOT OBTAINED', l. 360).

cards.title: Continuous integration passes, for the first time since the workflow was added
cards.statement: Every run of .github/workflows/check.yml failed from the moment it was added on 2026-09-21 until the repair commit of that afternoon: 24 runs, 0 successes, and because each of the two jobs stopped at its second step, the figure-reproducibility check and tools/check_rigor_builds.py had never executed once. Two unrelated causes. (1) The site-data step ran tools/build_site_data_extra.py --check, whose fourth payload, the claim map, is built from the knowledge base; that is a separate private repository the runner does not check out, so the script raised Drift and exited 2. It now takes --allow-missing-kb, which drops that one payload and checks the three built from result files in this repository; the skip prints the name of the unchecked file, and WITHOUT the flag a missing knowledge base is still an error, so a working clone cannot quietly stop checking the claim map. (2) The papers job failed compiling paper1, and the cause was isolated only afterwards, because the Makefile sent pdflatex's output to /dev/null and no run ever recorded the error. The missing package was lmodern, which carries lmodern.sty (/usr/share/texmf/tex/latex/lm/lmodern.sty); paper1/main.tex loads it on line 2, so with -halt-on-error nothing past line 2 was ever reached. The commit also names texlive-pictures, which was a no-op: it is a hard Depends of texlive-latex-extra and appears in the failing runs' own apt log ('Setting up texlive-pictures (2023.20240207-1)'), and --no-install-recommends suppresses Recommends, not Depends. fonts-lmodern, installed in both the failing and the passing runs, ships no .sty file. REF-CI-PAGES established this after the fact by diffing the apt 'NEW packages will be installed' lists of the last failing run (28 packages) and the first passing one (31: the same 28 plus lmodern, xfonts-encodings, xfonts-utils), not by reading a LaTeX error, which no run produced; the workflow comment at check.yml has been corrected to say this. The Makefile also sent pdflatex's output to /dev/null, so the log recorded a non-zero exit with no reason attached; on failure it now prints the last 40 lines of main.log. Separately, make rigor had never run at all: the target's name matches the rigor/ directory and was absent from .PHONY, so make reported it up to date and did nothing. The first success came on the repair commit: both jobs green, and check_rigor_builds.py reports 41 document(s), 0 failing, 0 known in a clone that carries no private material, which is the number README section 13 claims. The pages job ran for the first time on 2026-09-22, when decision D1's three conditions were met in order: the repository went public, Pages was enabled with this workflow as its build type, and the if: false was removed. Going public enabled nothing by itself, which is what rigor/public_site_plan.md:226 means by 'one line plus one click'; the click was a REST call with a user token, because creating a Pages site needs Administration (write) and GITHUB_TOKEN cannot carry it. configure-pages' enablement input could not have supplied the third, because its own action.yml at v5 requires a token other than GITHUB_TOKEN and Administration (write) is not a key of the workflow permissions: schema (REF-CI-PAGES-B); the job deploys an existing site and cannot create one. WHAT THE FLAG DOES NOT DO is protect CI: with the knowledge base absent a drifted docs/data/extra-claim-map.json is announced as unchecked and then waved through, and nothing on the runner can rebuild it, so only `make check` in a clone that has the knowledge base beside it will catch that, i.e. a human before committing. This is not hypothetical: at the commit before the regeneration the committed claim map was missing the ci-green and docs-pages-rendering nodes and six edges, and the next run was green over it (REF-CI-PAGES). It was regenerated in the following commit. The 24 failing runs and the first passing one were destroyed on 2026-09-21 when the remote was deleted and recreated to clear the compendia exposure; the run history now starts at the recreation, so the failure sequence is no longer checkable on GitHub and this Statement is the record of it.

cards.title: CMI as the data-processing defect of tracing out C (Note 2)
cards.statement: In finite dimensions I(A:C|B) = D(rho_ABC || rho_A x rho_BC) - D(rho_AB || rho_A x rho_B), the defect of the data-processing inequality for Tr_C (eq:cmi-dpi-defect); equality (Markov state) is equivalent to exact Petz recovery and to the Hayden-Jozsa-Petz-Winter decomposition (literature). In type III, for an inclusion N subset M and FAITHFUL NORMAL states rho, sigma on M with D_M(rho || sigma) < infinity (Note 2, l. 304 and 311-315), vanishing of the data-processing defect delta_{N subset M}(rho, sigma) = D_M(rho||sigma) - D_N(rho|N || sigma|N) is equivalent, by Petz's sufficiency theorem, to exact recovery by a normal unital 2-positive map alpha: M -> N with rho|N o alpha = rho and sigma|N o alpha = sigma (eq:petz-vn-equivalence), and, for faithful states, to the Connes-cocycle criterion [D rho : D sigma]_t in N for all real t (eq:connes-criterion, l. 317-321); without D_M(rho || sigma) < infinity the defect is infinity - infinity and the equivalence is not established. This is the reading that makes the recovery error a quantitative companion of the CMI.
cards.verify: cmi_as_quantum_markov_defect.tex eq:cmi-dpi-defect (l. 229-236), Petz/HJPW equivalences (l. 270-296, literature), type-III hypotheses and eq:petz-vn-equivalence (l. 304-315), eq:connes-criterion (l. 317-321); rigor/check_notes_1_2.tex.

cards.title: The first-order compression defect is a commutator with the vacuum symbol: ddelta = [Q, E_I D_chi E_I] (F1 Lemma 6.1)
cards.statement: With d := E_I D_chi E_I one has ddelta = E_I[P, D_chi]E_I = [Q, d], and on the isometric orbit the first-order defect is delta^(1)(zeta,0,0) = [Q, d - zeta] for anti-self-adjoint zeta = E_D zeta E_D, so the tangent problem is expressed through (Q, E_D) and the single operator d.

cards.title: E_rec <= (1-theta) f2 z^2 (1+o(1)): the zero-collar compression is NOT optimal in exact fidelity
cards.statement: PROVED (no numerical input): per chirality E_rec <= (1 - theta_fr) f2 z^2 (1+o(1)) (Thm 7.3), where theta_fr is the isometric-orbit gain sup over FINITE-RANK anti-self-adjoint G = E_D G E_D with v_G != 0; and theta_fr > 0 iff R_a != 0, equivalently (S10 Cor. 11.2: E_D u E_D is purely anti-self-adjoint) iff E_D u E_D != 0. Proof: the g_Q-free (UH) (card uhlmann-upper-half-proved) minimised in lambda and maximised in G, plus ||u||_2^2 = g_B/4 (S10 Prop. 4.3(2)) so (1/2)||u||^2 = f2. NUMERICAL: theta_fr >= 0.38, hence kappa_opt <= 0.616 +- 0.003 < 1, i.e. the zero-collar compression is beaten in EXACT fidelity, not merely in the second-order functional. The bridge from the published theta to theta_fr is Remark 7.4: (i) theta_fr = theta_HS by S_2-density of finite-rank anti-Hermitian G supported in D (all quantities depend on G only through P^perp G P, S_2-continuously), only theta_HS = theta (bounded G with P^perp G P in S_2 but G not in S_2) is open and is irrelevant for a LOWER bound; (ii) the explicit admissible HS direction G = R_a gives theta_fr >= 0.0143; (iii) every discretisation behind the numerical theta is finite-dimensional, so its optimisers are finite rank -- and F3's extrapolations are themselves taken over finite meshes, so theta_fr >= 0.38 is as well supported as theta = 0.384 +- 0.003 (Phase 5, F3, card theta-value; the modular Galerkin frame of S12 Sec. 5.2 and the parameter-free modular Wiener-Hopf frame of rigor/exact_optimum_tangent_problem.tex Prop 6.2 agree to 3e-4 after extrapolation; S10 Sec. 7's 0.300 +- 0.005 is a taper-suppressed LOWER bound). Wording updated in rigor/exact_fidelity_upper_half.tex Remark 7.4 (rem:thetafr) and the dated addendum to its Sec. 10. Sandwich (Cor 7.5): sup over admissible test families of liminf Delta_z(t_z)^2/(8 V(t_z) z^2) <= liminf E_rec/z^2 <= limsup E_rec/z^2 <= (1 - theta_fr) f2; the identification of the left side with D_z = min_F g_Q is S12 Thm 4.1(2) and is CONDITIONAL on a test family with ||t_z||_1^2/V(t_z) bounded and Delta_z(t_z)||t_z||_1/V(t_z) -> 0. Also note (referee R7): the structural chain is duality-free but the constant f2 reaches back to PA Prop. 7.6, hence to twisted duality.

cards.title: Corner calculus: sequential one-sided recovery = Schwarzian point masses at the junctions
cards.statement: One-sided zero-collar protocol on adjacent intervals A_1..A_n: step m adjoins A_new to the block J_{m-1} conditioning on a sub-block A_B adjacent to it, corner p^(m) = the end of A_B not shared with A_new, parabolic compression toward p^(m) with sigma_m = s_m/(l_B+l_new), s_m in [lambda_m, 2 lambda_m] (each step is the VACUUM Petz map of its own inclusion F(A_B) subset F(A_B u A_new), applied to whatever state the earlier steps produced); composite point map Phi = k_1 o ... o k_N (first step OUTERMOST). (1) GENERAL RULE, no hypothesis (Thm 5.2): Phi is C^1 piecewise-Moebius and S(Phi) = -2 sum_m sigma_m G_m'(x_m) delta_{x_m} -- with the DERIVATIVE G_m'(x_m), not G_m(x_m) -- where G_m := k_{m+1} o ... o k_N and x_m := G_m^{-1}(p^(m)); terms with p^(m) outside the range of G_m are absent (the corner is swallowed). (2) UNDER (H) (no earlier corner lies in the interior of a later step moving part A_B u A_new) (Thm 5.3): S(Phi) = -2 sum_k kappa_k delta_{p_k} over the INTERIOR junctions of J_N, kappa_k = sum of the sigmas of the steps whose corner is p_k; in particular S(Phi) is order independent. Sufficient for (H): (a) every A_B is a SINGLE chain interval AND the starting block has >= 2 chain intervals; (b) all corners coincide (VWZ 1(B)); (c) N = 1. CORRECTION (G1a): single-interval conditioning ALONE does not imply (H) -- Example 5.6, chain (1,1,1) started from the single interval A_2, add A_3 on A_2 then A_1 on A_2: the first corner is swallowed (not in the range of k_2), S(Phi) = -2 sigma_2 delta_{p_3} and Phi = (global Moebius) o k_2, so the first step leaves the state unchanged. (3) The composite algebra map is a normal *-isomorphism onto its range (Note 4 Thm 7.1 per step; Phi itself is NOT a single zero-collar map) and equals beta_{V_Phi} (V_{k_1}V_{k_2} = V_{k_1 o k_2}); the recovered state depends on Phi ONLY through S(Phi), because equal Schwarzians means Phi_2 = g o Phi_1 with g a global Moebius map (without pole on the OPEN interval Phi_1(J); the closure version is false) and omega o Ad U_g = omega (Thm 6.3). For a single corner the state, hence Phi_A, depends only on zeta = sigma beta_I(p) and not on the side of the compression (Cor 6.5). (4) RIGIDITY (Thm 7.3): omega o beta_Phi = omega on F(I) iff Phi is Moebius iff S(Phi) = 0; since all Schwarzian masses are negative and the last step is never swallowed, exact recovery never occurs for a protocol WHOSE LAST STEP KEEPS A NON-EMPTY PART (A_B strictly inside the block) -- unconditionally, without the second-order law. The hypothesis is needed: a degenerate step conditioning on the WHOLE block puts its corner on the boundary of I, where beta_I = 0, and is a pure Moebius compression that recovers the vacuum exactly (Rem 7.4; it is not a recovery in the Petz sense, since it keeps nothing fixed). (5) Consequences: VWZ 1(B) = 1(A) LITERALLY as point maps and for every common rotation t (2c/(b(b+c)) + 2d/((b+c)(b+c+d)) = 2(c+d)/(b(b+c+d))); VWZ Protocol 3 in either order is literally the same point map (parabolic L and R at the same point commute) and equals, up to post-composition with a global Moebius map, the over-compressed Theorem-A step with kept block AB, conditioning interval C, new interval D and s = (sigma_1+sigma_2)(c+d) > 2 lambda = 2d/c STRICTLY, hence Phi^(3) = Phi_A(zeta_eff), zeta_eff = (sigma_1+sigma_2)(a+b)(c+d)/(a+b+c+d); protocols with the same corner measure give the same state; and with single-interval conditioning the corner measure -- hence the holonomy -- depends only on the STARTING BLOCK, so the 2^{n-2} protocols starting from an adjacent pair fall into exactly n-1 classes, distinct pairs giving distinct measures (Prop 9.1 + Lem 9.2; tables for n = 4 and n = 5).

cards.title: Separation constraint: all-weak L->R Petz chains have e^{Delta_k} >= 2/eps (sharp)
cards.statement: L->R ordinary-Petz chain (start A_1A_2, adjoin A_{k+1} conditioning on A_k), corners p_2..p_{n-1}, kappa_k = 2 l_{k+1}/(l_k(l_k+l_{k+1})), zeta_k = kappa_k L_{k-1}(T-L_{k-1})/T, Delta_k = y_{k+1}-y_k the modular length of A_k (Delta_n := +infinity). EXACT IDENTITIES (Lem 10.3): zeta_k = sinh(Delta_{k+1}/2)/(sinh(Delta_k/2) sinh((Delta_k+Delta_{k+1})/2)), equivalently 1/zeta_k = sinh^2(Delta_k/2) coth(Delta_{k+1}/2) + (1/2) sinh(Delta_k) -- the corner strengths are functions of the MODULAR LENGTHS alone; consequently e^{Delta_k} <= 1 + 2/zeta_k, with equality IF AND ONLY IF k = n-1 (where Delta_n = infinity and coth = 1) and strict inequality for k <= n-2, the exact gap being 2 sinh^2(Delta_k/2)(coth(Delta_{k+1}/2) - 1); and (e^{Delta_k}-1) zeta_k = 2 r_k(1+v_k)/(1+r_k) >= 2 r_k/(1+r_k) (REF-P6-0 item 6). SEPARATION THEOREM (Thm 11.1): if zeta_j <= eps < 2 for every corner j >= k (only the corners to the RIGHT of p_k are used), then e^{Delta_k} >= 2/eps, and e^{Delta_{n-1}} >= 1 + 2/zeta_{n-1} >= 1 + 2/eps for the last corner. Proof: with gamma_j := coth(Delta_j/2) - 1 = 2/(e^{Delta_j}-1), the identity gives e^{Delta_j} >= 1 + 4/(zeta_j (2 + gamma_{j+1})), hence the recursion gamma_j <= zeta_j(1 + gamma_{j+1}/2); downward induction from gamma_n = 0 gives the fixed point gamma_j <= 2 eps/(2-eps), and substituting back gives e^{Delta_k} >= 1 + (4/eps)/(2 + 2 eps/(2-eps)) = 2/eps. SHARPNESS: only as eps -> 0. REF-P6-3 computed the EXACT constrained minimum of e^{Delta_k} by a closed backward recursion in the modular variables: 6.8134, 20.0499, 66.6817, 200.0050, 666.6682 at eps = 0.3, 0.1, 0.03, 0.01, 0.003, i.e. (eps/2) min = 1.0220, 1.0025, 1.00022, 1.000025, 1.000002 -- the bound is exceeded by 2.2% at eps = 0.3 and is approached only as eps -> 0. REF-P6-0s eps = 0.3 entry 6.75 lies BELOW the exact minimum 6.8134 and is a float-cancellation artifact (a naive search over the lengths destroys T - L_k); it is withdrawn. The hypothesis cannot be weakened to the pair {k,k+1}: with only that pair weak the separation stays O(1) (min e^{Delta} = 8.07 at eps = 0.01, REF-P6-3). GENERAL ADMISSIBLE CASE (Cor 11.2): with s_j in [lambda_j, 2 lambda_j], zeta_j <= eps < 1 for all j >= k gives e^{Delta_k} >= 1/eps.
cards.verify: rigor/g1a_separation.py (15 checks, all PASS, output a verbatim capture): the modular identities in 50000 random chains (max rel err 3.5e-10); e^{D_k} <= 1+2/zeta_k with 0 violations, the exact gap formula for k <= n-2, and EXACT equality at k = n-1 in all chains; the separation bound in 400000 random chains (min (eps/2)e^{D_k} = 0.999999996); the recursion and fixed point in 200000 chains; the admissible case; and the exact constrained minimum by backward recursion, reproducing 6.8134, 20.0499, 66.6817, 200.0050, 666.6682. cards.title: The generated documentation is rendered to HTML for Pages, with the Markdown still the source
cards.statement: GitHub Pages does not render Markdown: a .md file with no YAML front matter is a static file and is served verbatim, content-type text/markdown, with or without docs/.nojekyll, so a browser shows it as plain text or saves it. Every link from the interactive site into the generated documentation therefore landed a reader on a text file, 113 in 12 HTML files plus one built at runtime in claim-map.html from the JSON field 'page'. Removing .nojekyll is not the fix, because Jekyll converts only pages carrying front matter (a file without it is a static file and is never processed, so a defaults: block cannot rescue it) and front matter would then appear in the Markdown that GitHub renders when someone browses the repository. So the Markdown stays the source and gains a rendering. tools/md_to_html.py (stdlib only) writes docs/read/, one .html per .md, the same directory structure, so the directory prefix of a relative link between two documentation pages is preserved and only the suffix changes. THE SUBSET IS NOT CLOSED, and the card said the opposite twice before REF-CI-PAGES-B broke it twenty ways. reject_unsupported() is a BLACKLIST, so it makes the constructs it names loud and leaves the rest silent; it is a guard, not a proof. It now raises on an ordered list with either . or ) , a fenced block, a nested bullet, a + list, a setext underline, an underscore or spaced thematic break, a raw HTML block or an inline HTML tag, a closed ATX heading, a two-space or backslash line break, a doubled backtick, an HTML entity, an image, an autolink, a reference link, a link target carrying whitespace, a title or pointy brackets, strikethrough, triple emphasis in either delimiter, and a comment opened or closed inside a line; blocks() raises on an indented code block, a pipe table with no alignment row, a link target escaping the repository, an unterminated comment and text after a comment's close. ONE STRUCTURAL INVARIANT is checked rather than pattern-matched, and it is the one that was destroying content: every table row must have the header's cell count and a closing bar, so a row split where it should not have been raises instead of dropping its last cell. What is still silently wrong, none of it occurring in what the generator emits today and each found by REF-PASS-C probing the real pipeline: a table with no leading bars, a row missing its leading bar, lazy blockquote continuation, balanced parentheses in a link target, a --- line read as a rule where CommonMark would read a setext h2, and same-character emphasis nesting (*a **b** c*). A code span containing a backtick RAISES, and runs of three or more delimiters raise, so neither is in this list. Emphasis is STRICTER THAN CommonMark on purpose: a run may open only after the start of a line or whitespace and close only before the end of a line, whitespace or punctuation, with CommonMark's intraword rule kept for _. Conforming flanking is not good enough for this corpus, which is mathematics in plain text: under it a delimiter next to punctuation is a legal opener, so M_* loses four asterisks, $\|f\|_{\beta}$ loses its subscript underscores, and GitHub renders those files exactly that badly. The mirror is therefore deliberately MORE faithful to the mathematics than GitHub's own rendering of the same file, and the divergence is confined to emphasis. Three link classes occur and each has one answer on Pages, where only docs/ is published: another documentation page keeps its relative path with .md swapped for .html; a file elsewhere in the repository becomes an absolute blob URL, since it is not deployed; a directory gets its index, which is why read/results/index.html is generated (two pages link to results/ and Pages does not list directories). A fourth, per page and by design: each mirror page's footer links to its own .md source on github.com. The mirror is generated by build_docs.py, so --check covers it (a changed byte, a deleted mirror page, and an orphan anywhere under read/ including a nested one, verified by REF-CI-PAGES); 65 pages became 131 in total, namely 65 Markdown and 66 HTML. A page a human has taken over by the hand-edit marker is mirrored from what is on disk, because that is what a reader sees. FIDELITY. The rendered text loses no source word: all 65 pages match at alphanumeric-word granularity against two independent extractors and a markdown-it GFM baseline, and all 8 anchor ids survive as attributes. Word-level fidelity is not character-level fidelity, and REF-CI-PAGES found five character-level defects in the mirror as first committed, all repaired and each verified against the source line; REF-CI-PAGES-B then found that the repair itself had introduced two more, both now fixed: history.md:143 lost both adjoint stars of 'N = 1 - XX* >= 0 ... X* <= N' to a spurious em (fixed by flanking); _underscore_ emphasis was unimplemented and showed as literal underscores on 28 of 66 pages (fixed, 27 result pages now render it as emphasis); title_of() de-escaped by stripping [`*] from raw Markdown, so three titles disagreed with their own h1 (fixed by rendering the heading to plain text); notation.md:119,123 became 5- and 9-cell rows in a 3-column table because tabular_to_md escaped every pipe and so turned a LaTeX norm bar \| into \\|, an escaped backslash followed by a live delimiter (fixed upstream by escaping only unescaped pipes; both rows are 3 cells); history.md:219 became a 10-cell row in a 2-column table because a table copied verbatim out of rigor/PHASE5_STATUS.md carries bare pipes inside a code span, which GFM splits on (fixed upstream by pipes_in_code_spans(); the row is 2 cells and ||u||^2 is intact). LaTeX norm bars still degrade to single bars in these tables, as they do on GitHub, because the mirror ships no math renderer. Also repaired here: check_links.py was applying the Markdown link pattern to HTML too, where mathematics like [h''/h'](p) arrives as rendered text with its backslashes already resolved, and reported three links that do not exist; the pattern now applies to Markdown only. README carries the Pages address six times, three in the introduction (lines 29, 35, 36; section 1 begins at 40) and three in section 9 (337, 338, 339; the section runs 307 to 349). It no longer explains what publication requires: that paragraph was written for a private repository and was removed on 2026-09-22 at the user's instruction, because a published README does not need it. From 2026-09-21 the README pointed at an address that did not serve, and from the morning of 2026-09-22 it said nothing about that either; the repository was private until the flip on 2026-09-22, so until then the only readers were its owner and, from 14:35 UTC that day, the one collaborator added that afternoon; the flip was the first of the three steps and so came before the address served, and for that last stretch -- somewhere between 14:35 and 21:28 UTC, which is as closely as the feeds date the flip -- the non-serving address was in a world-readable README. All three publication steps landed on 2026-09-22 and the address serves. What publication required is recorded in decision D1, in the workflow comment and on ci-green: the repository going public, the if: false on the Pages job removed, and Pages enabled once on the repository. All three were done on 2026-09-22 and the mirror is live: the site root, read/index.html, read/status.html and read/results/index.html all return 200 and text/html, which is what this whole module exists to make true. configure-pages has an enablement input, but its own action.yml at the pinned ref v5 requires a token other than GITHUB_TOKEN, because creating the site needs Administration (write) and that is not a key of the workflow permissions: schema, so it cannot do the third step and is not set. cards.title: Exact -1/2 log det(1-V^*V) with the optimised extension confirms (UH) beyond first order
cards.statement: With the Tikhonov-optimised exterior generator Z_e (mu = 1e-8; the mu = 1e-4 rows overshoot by 3e-3 and are not used) and W~ = exp(Z_pre + Z_e), Z_pre = -s D_chi resp. -s(D_chi + eps_* G_*), the EXACT Uhlmann exponent UH = -(1/2) log det(1 - V^*V), V = P^perp W~ P (singular values, log1p), satisfies at L = 128..384 and s = 0.001, 0.002, 0.005: UH_compr / ((1/2) s^2 |u|^2) between 1.00000 (s = 0.001) and 0.99981 (s = 0.005, L = 384), i.e. equal to the first-order UB to within 2e-4, the deficit a clean O(s^2); UH_rot / ((1/2) s^2 |u|^2) = 0.70885 (L=128), 0.71125 (192), 0.71057 (256), 0.70764 (384) at s = 0.001, against 1 - theta = 0.70890, 0.71120, 0.71051, 0.70767: agreement to about 5e-5, i.e. four significant digits; decreasing slightly with s (0.70714 at s = 0.005, L = 384). The two second-order-inequivalent constructions exp(Z_pre) exp(Z_e) and W_s exp(-s eps_* G_*) exp(Z_e) give values below the sum version (0.70596 and 0.70810 at L = 128, s = 0.001). Hence (UH) holds in this model beyond first order, with room to spare.

cards.title: NS-circle model: Ext = N^perp exactly, with the dimension identity (L-|I|)^2
cards.statement: In S10's spectral NS-circle model (exact Hardy projection P of rank k = L/2, I = A u D an arc of m = |I| sites, m > L/2) both spanning maps are DIAGONALISED exactly: with Q = E_I P E_I (eigenvalues q, basis U) one has E_I(P^perp l P + P l P^perp)E_I = (1-Q) l Q + Q l (1-Q), so ||P^perp l P||_2^2 = (1/2) sum_ij den_ij |l_ij|^2 with den_ij = q_i(1-q_j)+q_j(1-q_i); likewise for Z anti-Hermitian on I^c with Qc = E_{I^c} P E_{I^c}. Hence dim_R N = m^2 - 2 z^2 with z = m - L/2 (rank Q = rank(1-Q) = L/2 forces z exact zero and z exact unit eigenvalues, and den vanishes exactly on the (0,0) and (1,1) pairs), dim_R S_2(PH,P^perp H) = L^2/2, and dim_R N^perp = L^2/2 - m^2 + 2z^2 = (L/2 - z)^2 = (L-m)^2 = dim_R Ext. Together with L1 (Ext subset N^perp) this gives Ext = N^perp EXACTLY at every L. Brute-force verification with explicit real bases at L = 32, 48: ranks 316/196 and 711/441 match the formula exactly and all principal angles between Ext and N^perp are 0 (cos = 1.0000000000 to 10 digits); at L = 64 double precision loses 22 of 1319 dimensions of N to roundoff but all principal angles are still 0.
cards.verify: run numerics/optimality_all/e2_subspaces.py; part (A) prints 'cos(angle) min=1.0000000000' and ranks equal to the predicted m^2-2z^2 and (L-m)^2

cards.title: Optimised exterior extension: UB_c = (1/2)s^2|u|^2 exactly and UB_rot/UB_c = 1-theta
cards.statement: In the NS-circle model (a = 2, Lg = 1, uv = (0.30,0.42), alpha = 3) with the exterior generator OPTIMISED (least squares over all anti-Hermitian Z_e supported on I^c, solved in closed form by the Qc-eigenbasis diagonalisation): UB(X) = (1/2) dist(X, Ext)^2 = (1/2)(||Pi X||^2 + dist((1-Pi)X, Ext)^2). Numerically dist((1-Pi)M, Ext)^2 and dist((1-Pi)v, Ext)^2 are at roundoff (|d^2| <= 1.3e-10 against ||(1-Pi)M||^2 = 2.45e-2, relative distance <= 1.2e-5 and usually exactly 0 in double precision) for L = 128, 192, 256, 384. Hence UB_c/((1/2)s^2|u|^2) = 1.00000000, 0.99999999, 1.00000000, 0.99999998 at L = 128, 192, 256, 384 -- this REPLACES the 4.3 of the fixed Gaussian-taper extension (numerics/optimality_all/uhlmann_rotated.py), a factor 4.3 that was entirely an artefact of a bad exterior extension. And UB_rot/UB_c = 0.70885, 0.71125, 0.71058, 0.70766, equal to 1 - theta = 0.70890, 0.71120, 0.71051, 0.70767 to 4-5 digits. UB is exactly quadratic in s, so the ratios are s-independent to machine precision (checked at s = 0.001, 0.002, 0.005). eps_* = -1.0000 in units of s, as predicted by <u,v_x> = ||v_x||^2 = <b,x>.

cards.title: Is the compression beaten in EXACT fidelity?
cards.statement: ANSWERED 2026-09-15 (Phase 4): yes, modulo one numerical input. Proved (rigor/exact_fidelity_upper_half.tex, refereed 'stands with repairs', repairs applied): exterior directions are dense in the invisible space (Thm 5.3), so the optimised Uhlmann bound equals the second-order functional for every isometric quasi-free channel (Thm 4.3, Cor 4.4, Thm 7.1 in g_Q-free form) and E_rec <= (1 - theta_fr) f2 z^2 (1+o(1)) per chirality (Thm 7.3), with theta_fr > 0 iff E_D u E_D is not self-adjoint. Lower half: E_rec >= the unconditional dual form of optimality_all_channels.tex eq. (10); the sharper statement E_rec >= D_z (1-o(1)) is conditional on an admissible test family (Cor 7.5 of the E1 document, referee repair R5). cards.title: Exterior directions exhaust the invisible space: closure(Ext) = N^perp (question (Q) settled, YES)
cards.statement: In the real Hilbert space S_2(PH, P^perp H) with inner product Re Tr(X^* Y), let N = {P^perp l P : l = l^* = E_I l E_I} (visible space) and Ext = {P^perp Z_e P : Z_e^* = -Z_e = E_{I^c} Z_e E_{I^c}} (exterior directions). Then closure(Ext) = N^perp = {B : E_I(B + B^*)E_I = 0}, and finite-rank Z_e already suffice. Proof (invariant, no Halmos normal form): B orthogonal to both spaces means, with Xi := B + B^*, Gamma := 2P-1: Gamma Xi + Xi Gamma = 0, E_I Xi E_I = 0, E_{I^c} Gamma Xi E_{I^c} = 0. Compressing Gamma Xi Gamma = -Xi with E_{I^c} and inserting 1 = E_I + E_{I^c} twice gives Gamma' pi Gamma' = pi with pi = E_{I^c} Xi E_{I^c}, Gamma' = E_{I^c}(2P-1)E_{I^c}; since Gamma' is a self-adjoint contraction with no eigenvalue +-1 (generic position) Gamma'^n -> 0 strongly, and pi is compact, so pi = 0; then E_{I^c} P E_I (E_I Xi E_{I^c}) = 0 with E_{I^c} P E_I injective gives Xi = 0. FINITE-RANK exterior generators already suffice (closure(Ext_fr) = closure(Ext) = N^perp). Compactness of the test element is NOT needed (referee R3): for any BOUNDED pi with pi = Gamma'^n pi Gamma'^n one has |<xi, pi eta>| <= ||Gamma'^n xi|| ||pi|| ||Gamma'^n eta|| -> 0, so pi = 0 by two-sided strong convergence alone; the earlier claim that bounded solutions exist (from approximate eigenvectors) is false, since approximate eigenvectors at +-1 tend weakly to 0. Generic position IS essential: one failure in each of the two groups breaks it (f in h_{I^c} cap PH and g in h_I cap P^perp H give B = |g><f| nonzero in N^perp cap Ext^perp). Only a CLOSURE is claimed because Z_e -> P^perp Z_e P has unbounded inverse on N^perp (E2 Sec. 2.3), not because of the fixed-point equation. Second, independent proof: N and Ext are the (1,1)-sector standard subspaces of F(I) and F(I)', so (Q) IS Haag/twisted duality (Tomita: K^perp_R = i K').

cards.title: Finite chains: exterior directions span exactly the invisible space (Ext = N^perp)
cards.statement: On the half-filled hopping chain with P the Fermi projection and I a contiguous block (n = 8..16, |I| = 3..7), the real span N of the visible directions P^perp l P (l Hermitian on I) has dimension |I|^2, the span Ext of the exterior directions P^perp Z P (Z anti-Hermitian on I^c) is orthogonal to N and has dimension 2k(n-k) - |I|^2, and N + Ext is all of S_2(PH, P^perp H): Ext = N^perp exactly in every case. Algebraically, B = P^perp X P is orthogonal to N iff E_I(B + B^*)E_I = 0 and to Ext iff E_{I^c}(B - B^*)E_{I^c} = 0; with H = B + B^* (Hermitian, P-off-diagonal) and S = 1 - 2P one has B - B^* = S H, so (Q) is the two-projection statement: a P-off-diagonal Hermitian H with E_I H E_I = 0 and E_{I^c} S H E_{I^c} = 0 vanishes. This is the finite-dimensional shadow of question (Q) of the Phase 4 brief; the continuum statement (density, Hardy projection, interval) is track E1's target.

cards.title: Amplification: the corner strength in the chain frame is zeta_step (1 + z')
cards.statement: For a corner (p, sigma) and two intervals I_step subset I containing p, the strengths zeta^(I') = sigma beta_{I'}(p) (beta_{I'}(x) = (x-alpha)(omega-x)/(omega-alpha), the modular-frame density of I' = (alpha,omega)) satisfy zeta^(I) >= zeta^(I_step), with equality iff I = I_step, because beta_{(alpha,omega)}(p) is increasing in omega and decreasing in alpha. If the step's kept block reaches the left end of the chain, I_step = (p_1, f) with f the far end of the moving part, then zeta^(I)/zeta^(I_step) = beta_I(p)/beta_{I_step}(p) = (a+b)(b+c)/(b(a+b+c)) = 1 + z' with a = p - p_1, b = f - p, c = p_{n+1} - f; z' = ac/(b(a+b+c)) is simultaneously the cross ratio of (p_1, p, f, p_{n+1}) and paper 1's Markov variable z of the coarse triple (kept block | A_B u A_new | rest of the chain). z' >= 0, and z' = 0 iff f = p_{n+1}, i.e. iff the step is the last one. Underlying exact fact (Lem 3.3, 3.4): the parabolic parameter is a (-1)-density, sigma' = sigma/M'(p) under a Moebius change of coordinate, so zeta = sigma beta_I(p) is Moebius invariant and is exactly the coefficient of w(y-y_p) = -4 sinh^2((y-y_p)/2) 1_{y>y_p} in the first-order field in the modular frame of I; for I = (-a,L), p = 0, sigma = s/L it is paper 1's zeta = as/(a+L).

cards.title: Full primal SDP over F in the modular Galerkin frame: min_F g_Q = 8.41 and 7.13 times g_Q(delta_c) at h = 0.4, 0.3 -- the S11 representability obstruction, not a statement about non-isometric channels
cards.statement:
In the block-exact modular Galerkin frame of kkt_continuum.py (a = 1, L = 2, Lambda = 12, s = 0.1, kind = 'first'), the full primal SDP over F = {X : h_B -> h_D, Z = Z* : X Q_BB X* <= Z <= 1 - X(1-Q_BB)X*} was solved at two rungs (f2_galerkin_a.out; 9425 s at h = 0.4, 24923 s at h = 0.3):
h = 0.4, N = 69, (nA,nB,nC) = (30,9,30): g_Q(delta_c) = 8.1495e-06 = 0.8687 f2 zeta^2, theta = 0.28578, min_F g_Q = 6.8546e-05, min_F/g_Q(delta_c) = 8.411034, ||1 - X X*||_F = 5.872, tr(1 - X X*) = 35.16 of m = 39, ||Z - X Q_BB X*||_F = 3.556, sv(X) in [0.0061, 0.9999];
h = 0.3, N = 91, (nA,nB,nC) = (40,11,40): g_Q(delta_c) = 8.4021e-06 = 0.8956 f2 zeta^2, theta = 0.29926, min_F g_Q = 5.9870e-05, min_F/g_Q(delta_c) = 7.125692, ||1 - X X*||_F = 6.780, tr(1 - X X*) = 46.71 of m = 51, sv(X) in [0.0002, 0.9999].
Both rungs land a factor 7-8 ABOVE the compression defect, not below the isometric-orbit value, and the optimal X is a strong contraction, nothing like a co-isometry.
WHAT IS BEING COMPARED (do not over-read the ratio): min_F g_Q is an exact finite-s minimum over the discretised F, whereas theta, 1 - theta and g_Q(delta_c) on the same rung are FIRST-ORDER (tangent) reference numbers produced by orbit_theta() (the CG of theta_galerkin.py, which it reproduces exactly: 1 - theta = 0.71422 at h = 0.4 and 0.70074 at h = 0.3 against the published 0.714 and 0.701). The two are not values of one and the same programme -- they are computed in one script and share Q and delta_c, but not the same optimisation -- so the ratio must not be read as "the orbit beaten or not beaten by that factor".
WHAT THE RUNGS DO SHOW is the S11 representability obstruction (rigor/sdp_certificate_numerics.tex l.484-497): in a finite Galerkin cell frame the Moebius compression is not representable at all (its V maps cells to non-cells), so the discretised F does not contain the compression point, and min_F g_Q is dominated by that representation error rather than by the physics of non-isometric channels.
H-TREND: the two rungs move in the right direction at fixed Lambda and collar, 8.411034 (h = 0.4) -> 7.125692 (h = 0.3). Two points are a trend, not a verdict, and no extrapolated "factor still to be closed" is claimed. The earlier runs kc_h04.out and kc_h05.out (8.2635 and 10.0467) are NOT comparable rungs of the same ladder: they differ in LamC (6 and 4 vs 12), n_B (9 and 7 vs 9 and 11) and n_C (15 and 8 vs 30 and 40); S11 identifies n_B/n_C and the collar s, not h alone, as the knobs, and kc_h04.out's Delta/(2 g_Q) = -10.325 is S11's n_B < n_C corner.
CONCLUSION: this test cannot decide whether non-isometric channels beat the isometric orbit; the tangent (first-order) problem is the right place to ask, and it is answered in the card kkt-noise-criterion-numerics.

cards.statement: For the massless Dirac field (lattice Dirac chain), with a gap G between A and B, I(A:C|B) = (1/3) log[(a+g+b)(g+b+c)/((g+b)(a+g+b+c))] exactly (adjacent formula with L_B -> L_B + L_G), so I ~ L_G^-2; -log F decays with the same power and -log F / I -> 0.09. cards.title: Hypothesis (U) is false: the natural-cone inner product is not the fidelity
cards.statement: REFUTED. Hypothesis (U) of rigor/network_corner_calculus.tex (Hyp. 12.1, hyp:U, l. 1729-1735) asserts that in the standard form (H, J, P) of a sigma-finite von Neumann algebra any two normal states phi, psi satisfy F(phi, psi) = sqrt(P_tr(phi, psi)) = <xi_phi, xi_psi>, with xi_phi, xi_psi their natural-cone representatives. This is false already for M = M_2. Standard form: H = M_2 with the Hilbert-Schmidt inner product, left multiplication, J x = x^*, natural cone = positive matrices; the cone representative of the state with density rho is rho^{1/2}, so <xi_rho, xi_sigma> = Tr(rho^{1/2} sigma^{1/2}), while F = Tr|rho^{1/2} sigma^{1/2}| (the document's F = P_tr^{1/2}, Box [G4]). Counterexamples: (i) pure states |0><0| and |+><+|: <xi, eta> = |<0|+>|^2 = 1/2 = F^2, whereas F = 1/sqrt 2 = 0.7071; (ii) faithful rho = diag(0.9, 0.1), sigma = [[0.5, 0.4], [0.4, 0.5]]: <xi, eta> = (sqrt 0.9 + sqrt 0.1)^2/2 = 0.8, whereas F = 0.8246. In general Tr(rho^{1/2} sigma^{1/2}) <= ||rho^{1/2} sigma^{1/2}||_1 = F, with equality iff rho^{1/2} sigma^{1/2} >= 0, i.e. iff rho and sigma commute; and F^2 <= <xi, eta> on all 20000 random M_2 pairs of the check. What holds in standard form is the supremum formula F(phi, psi) = sup over unitaries u' of M' of |<xi_phi, u' xi_psi>| (Alberti-Uhlmann 2002, Thm 2(3)). The project itself says that the natural cone does not compute the fidelity (universality_normalization.tex:277). The document attributes (U) to Araki-Raggio [AR82], 'A remark on transition probability', Lett. Math. Phys. 6 (1982) 237-240 (network_corner_calculus.tex:1737, :2194-2196; marked NOT OBTAINED there, not in refs/). That paper gives the supremum over vector representatives, not (U). The companion paper G. A. Raggio, Lett. Math. Phys. 6 (1982) 233-236, compares Uhlmann's transition probability with the natural-cone one and proves the inequality P <= <xi, eta> <= P^{1/2}. These are bibliographic checks by referees REF-DEP-CFT-B1 and B3; neither paper is in refs/. (U) is also used as a fact, undeclared, in rigor/check_notes_1_2.tex lem:fvdg <1>1 (l. 914-916) and in rigor/check_note4.tex l. 1621-1626. Both of those conclusions survive via FHSW Lemma 3(3) (REF-DEP-CFT-B3). Consequence: statements conditional on (U) are vacuous; in the project these are the angle form Thm 12.5 (thm:w6) and eq:w6-master (card sequential-recovery-angle-form-under-u); the chordal and second-order forms (card sequential-recovery-bound-type-iii) do not use (U).

By hand for (ii): sigma^{1/2} = [[p, q], [q, p]] with p = (sqrt 0.9 + sqrt 0.1)/2, q = (sqrt 0.9 - sqrt 0.1)/2, so Tr(rho^{1/2} sigma^{1/2}) = p (sqrt 0.9 + sqrt 0.1) = 0.8.

cards.title: Exact KKT certificate at the compression; Moebius rigidity
cards.statement: For a fixed self-adjoint TRACE-CLASS t on h_I (Thm. thm:kkt is stated for trace-class t, rigor/sdp_dual_certificate.tex:176): in the continuum V_c: h_D -> h_B is unitary, both LMIs are active, and the multipliers are unique: Sigma_1 = t_DA Q_AB V_c - t_DD V_c*(1-Q_BB)V_c, Sigma_2 = Sigma_1 + t_DD; the compression maximises Tr(t Q_rec) over F iff Sigma_1 = Sigma_1* >= 0 and Sigma_1 + t_DD >= 0 (Thm. thm:kkt; necessary and sufficient, no constraint qualification). Legendre reduction (Lemma lem:offdiag): V(t) = ||P^perp t P||^2, and Tr(t delta_c) depends on t only through N = P^perp t P. Moebius rigidity (Lemma lem:rigid): the DD block of the first-order compression defect vanishes, E_D ddelta E_D = [p, d] = 0 (the Moebius generator commutes with P and is local), hence E_D u E_D is purely anti-self-adjoint (Cor. cor:maximal), u the Riesz vector of the compression direction. At leading order in s (t = s tau, tau fixed; Lemma lem:sigma0, Prop. prop:split) the certificate is equivalent to (S) E_D N E_D self-adjoint together with (P) -E_D tau_{++} E_D <= E_D N E_D <= -E_D tau_{--} E_D, and for the compression's test operator (S) is the self-adjointness of E_D u E_D, i.e. (S) holds iff E_D u E_D = 0 (Thm. thm:obstruction, Cor. cor:maximal). PROVED consequence, the 'only if' half at leading order in s: a certificate at t_c requires E_D u E_D = 0. NOT PROVED, the 'if' half (E_D u E_D = 0 => a certificate at t_c exists): it needs (P) to be satisfiable, which Cor. cor:Pfree shows only for bounded E_D N E_D (in general kappa must be unbounded, t is then not trace class, and the regularisation is not pursued: verdict gap :450-459 and Verdict gap (iv) :956-958), and cor:Pfree changes the P-diagonal blocks of t, so it certifies a modified t with the same N, not t_c itself. Cor. cor:test applies thm:kkt to the SLD t_c without showing that t_c is trace class. Whether E_D u E_D = 0 is not decided here: numerically ||E_D u E_D||_2^2/||u||_2^2 = 0.0143 != 0 (S10 N1, eq:thetalb; card compression-not-second-order-minimiser), so, numerically and not by proof, the certificate fails at the compression.

cards.title: KKT criterion numerics: every finite run FAILS (a); the violation extrapolates to 0^- as h -> 0, Ymax -> inf; under H3, (e) follows from the proved E(zeta_inf) >= 0 alone, and the finite-h junction values are positive
cards.statement:
Numerical evaluation of the F1 Thm 4.4 criterion for the tangent problem (orbit = global optimum iff (a) M_* >= 0 and M_* - tau_* >= 0, and (e) the endpoint functional E(zeta) >= 0 for every admissible zeta with A(zeta,0,0) in the form domain F (thm:kktmain(e), exact_optimum_tangent_problem.tex:796-798), which on F1's model cone reads E(zeta_0) >= 0 and E(zeta_inf) >= 0; t_* is the SLD normalised by g_Q(delta_*) = (1/4) Tr(t_* delta_*), tau_* = E_D t_* E_D, M_* = Herm((t_* Q)_DD)). READ THE SIGN CLAIM AS AN EXTRAPOLATION: at every finite discretisation the run prints "CRITERION (M>=0 and M-tau>=0): False" (f2_t4_h024.out l.4, f2_t4_hladder.out l.4 and l.12, f2_t4_h003.out l.4, every Ymax row of f2_t4_ymax12.out); what the numerics establish is that the violation scales to zero in the double limit, with clean power laws, while the endpoint functional is positive at every finite discretisation (the regularised junction test, rem:H3space(2), tex :1223-1227); under hyp:H3, (e) holds outright from the proved E(zeta_inf) >= 0 (rem:H3space).
(1) PRIMARY FRAME, parameter-free modular Wiener-Hopf (F1 Prop 6.2 as built by F3 in f3_t0.py; I = (-inf,1), y = -log(1-x), A = {y<0}, D = {y>0}, Q exact in the cell basis, ddot in closed form, Moebius rigidity EXACT: ||ddot_DD|| = 0 identically). Structural checks all pass: SLD identity (1/4)Tr(t_* delta_*)/g_Q(delta_*) = 1.0000000000; ||AntiHerm((t_* Q)_DD)||/||M_*|| = 2.8e-9, 8.5e-8, 1.5e-7, 3.5e-7 at h = 0.24, 0.12, 0.06, 0.03; F1's derivative formula d g_Q = (1/2)[Tr(N1 M_*) - Tr(Y1 tau_*)] verified by central finite differences to <= 3e-8 (measured relative errors 3.94e-10, 1.08e-08, 7.56e-09, 2.63e-08 at h = 0.24, 0.12, 0.06, 0.03: f2_t4_h024.out l.5, f2_t4_hladder.out l.5 and l.13, f2_t4_h003.out l.5); theta reproduces F3's ladder (0.31367, 0.34236, 0.35934, 0.36945 at h = 0.24, 0.12, 0.06, 0.03, Y = Ymax = 10).
(a) SCALING OF THE VIOLATION. h-ladder at Y = Ymax = 10: lam_min(M_*)/||M_*|| = -4.076e-3, -1.859e-3, -8.228e-4, -3.667e-4 at h = 0.24, 0.12, 0.06, 0.03 (ratios 2.19, 2.26, 2.24 per halving, i.e. ~ h^1.15), and lam_min(M_* - tau_*) equals lam_min(M_*) to 5 digits (different eigenvectors with the same localisation and modulus profile and opposite <p,tau_*p>: at h = 0.24, <p,M_*p> = -5.4316e-4 and +2.7654e-3, <p,tau_*p> = -3.3086e-3 and +3.3086e-3, f2_t4_h024.out l.6-7). Outer-cutoff scan at h = 0.12, Y = 6: lam_min(M_*)/||M_*|| = -3.014e-3, -2.286e-3, -1.865e-3, -1.339e-3, -9.459e-4, -6.360e-4 for Ymax = 6, 8, 10, 14, 20, 30, i.e. lam_min/||M_*|| * Ymax = -0.0181, -0.0183, -0.0186, -0.0187, -0.0189, -0.0191 (~ 1/Ymax), and the rank-one gain Delta^2/g_Q(eta) in units of g_Q(ddot) = 3.325e-4, 1.874e-4, 1.230e-4, 6.236e-5, 3.080e-5, 1.380e-5 with gain * Ymax^2 = 0.0120 ... 0.0124 (~ 1/Ymax^2); on the h-ladder the same gain is 3.85e-4, 1.23e-4, 3.51e-5, 9.69e-6 (~ h^1.85). So lam_min(M_*)/||M_*|| ~ -c(h)/Ymax with c(0.24) = 0.041, c(0.12) = 0.0187 (c ~ h^1.1), and the gain ~ c'(h)/Ymax^2 with c'(0.24) = 0.039, c'(0.12) = 0.0123: both -> 0 in the double limit h -> 0, Ymax -> infinity, i.e. lam_min -> 0^- (a marginal, not a strict, sign). The violating eigenvector p supports this reading: in the Ymax scans at fixed h it is a delocalised mode at y ~ (0.37-0.6) Ymax (0.37 Ymax at Ymax = 30), tracking the artificial outer end of the y window (the moving endpoint x = 1); the A-side cutoff is irrelevant (Y = 6, 10, 14 give lam_min/||M_*|| = -1.8645e-3, -1.8586e-3, -1.8584e-3 at h = 0.12, Ymax = 10: the Y-scan block of f2_t5_endpoint.out, l.102, l.112, l.122; the h = 0.24 triple -4.0904e-3, -4.0756e-3, -4.0751e-3 is reported in F2_RESULTS.md:306, and of it only the Y = 10 value -4.0756e-3 is in an output file, f2_t4_h024.out l.2). At fixed Ymax = 10 the mode moves inward as h falls (y ~ 5.5, 5.1, 4.3, 1.9) while its eigenvalue keeps shrinking; the two vanishing scalings, not the location, carry the conclusion.
(e) ENDPOINT CONDITION (T5, f2_t5_endpoint.out). E(zeta) = 2 b(delta_*, A(zeta,0,0)) = (1/2)Tr(t_* A(zeta,0,0)) with A from F1 eq:Ablocks. Convention check, exact to machine precision at all four h: E(zeta_inf)/g_Q(ddot) = (1/2)Tr(t_* ddot)/g_Q(ddot) = 1.37265519, 1.31527744, 1.28132522, 1.26109117 (f2_t5_endpoint.out l.3, 13, 23, 33) against 2(1-theta_h) = same to 2e-16..1e-15; the identity E(zeta_inf) = 2 lambda (1-theta) g_Q(ddot) is proved (F1 Prop 4.10 <1>4), its positivity needs theta < 1, which is numerical (theta_h = 0.314-0.369 here). For zeta_0 = -E_D d/dy E_D discretised on the uniform D-mesh, only the backward (upwind) difference is the admissible shift semigroup (sigma = Herm(zeta_0) <= 0); it gives a TOTAL E(zeta_0)/g_Q(ddot) = +34.122, +66.873, +131.298, +257.998 at h = 0.24, 0.12, 0.06, 0.03, but that total is the scheme-DEPENDENT quantity: the discrete boundary form decomposes as E(zeta_0) = (1/2)[M_*(0,0) + h Tr((-Laplacian) M_*) + M_*(Ymax,Ymax)] and the total (~ h^-0.97) is dominated by the O(h) upwind-viscosity middle term, an artefact of the difference scheme. The scheme-invariant piece, the one that represents the continuum E(zeta_0) (tex :1169, :1588), is the CORNER row (1/2)(M_*)_00/h = +10.304, +16.096, +24.672, +37.210 (~ h^-0.60); it diverges, and it is the value quoted below for the regularised (finite-h) junction directions. The centred difference is exactly anti-Hermitian (sigma = 0, lies in L-bar) and gives E = 0 to 2e-5; the forward difference has sigma >= 0 (decompression, inadmissible) and gives the negative of the backward value. Both quantities saturate in Ymax (E_bwd = +66.90, +67.07, +67.23, +67.36, +67.45 and corner = +16.46, +16.15, +16.03, +15.95, +15.89 for Ymax = 6, 10, 14, 20, 30 at h = 0.12 and Y = 6, the T5b scan) and are independent of Y (+67.07, +66.87, +66.87 for Y = 6, 10, 14). The corner term does NOT saturate in h (it grows like h^-0.6), i.e. M_*(y,y) diverges as y -> 0+ and E(zeta_0) = +infinity in the sense of the second case of eq:Efun (A(zeta_0,0,0) not in F): a convention, not a margin (tex :1033-1037). Cross-check (ii): the first-cell diagonal of M_*/h is +0.160, +0.261, +0.409, +0.623 (same sign as E(zeta_0)) and the last-cell diagonal is +3.2e-3, +3.9e-3, +4.4e-3, +4.8e-3 (the last at h = 0.03, f2_t5_endpoint.out l.40; same sign as E(zeta_inf) > 0). VERDICT ON (e), QUALIFIED: the document's reading applies. The corner row diverges, so A(zeta_0,0,0) is not in F and E(zeta_0) = +infinity: (e) is VACUOUS at zeta_0 rather than satisfied with a margin (exact_optimum_tangent_problem.tex:1171-1176, :1591-1593). In the model-cone form E(zeta_0) > 0, the corner row is +10.3, +16.1, +24.7, +37.2 g_Q(ddot) at h = 0.24, 0.12, 0.06, 0.03, with no sign change at any h, Y, Ymax, and E(zeta_inf) = 2(1-theta_h) g_Q(ddot) (the proved identity) > 0 because theta_h < 1 numerically. At finite h the absorption identity E(zeta_0) = (1/2)Tr((-2 sigma) M_*) holds to <= 7.5e-8 (f2_t5_endpoint.out l.7, 17, 27, 37), but M_* >= 0 fails in every run and -2 sigma has full rank, so the positive sign is a numerical fact, not a forced one; in the continuum the identity is not available (prop:bdryfun(5), tex :1094-1096). Under hyp:H3 (tex :1191-1198), read in F, alpha = 0 is forced because A(zeta_0,0,0) is not in F: every admissible generator carrying a feasible first-order datum is, modulo L-bar, a non-negative multiple of zeta_inf, and (e) holds outright from E(zeta_inf) >= 0 alone (rem:H3space, :1209-1218). H3 is a hypothesis, not something these numerics test. So: numerically (a) in the limit; E(zeta_0) > 0 and E(zeta_inf) > 0; (e) for the whole cone under H3.
CAVEAT ON THE PRIMARY FRAME. It needs no weight cap at the h computed, but the weights are not bounded uniformly in h: kappa_max = 5.38, 6.51, 7.66, 8.84 and max w = 1.09e2, 3.36e2, 1.07e3, 3.44e3 at h = 0.24, 0.12, 0.06, 0.03 (ratios ~3.1-3.2 per halving, i.e. max w ~ h^-1.65). So h -> 0 is exactly the limit in which this frame's weights diverge as well; the extrapolation above is over a window in which max w grows by a factor 32, and a much finer h would eventually re-enter the regime where the T2 artefact mechanism (below) operates.
(2) SECONDARY FRAME, ARTEFACT-SUSPECT, S10 spectral circle model: the criterion FAILS at every L = 64, 96, 128, 192, 256, with lam_min(M_*)/||M_*|| = -0.206, -0.0075, -0.0352, -0.0579, -0.0498 and lam_min(M_* - tau_*) equal to it to 3 digits (at L = 96, 128, 192 only 3 digits agree, f2_kkt_f1_L.out l.43-45). That verdict must NOT be used, for three reasons, all in F1's normalisation as printed by f2_capscan.py (file f2_capscan_L128.out; the half-SLD convention of kkt_continuum.gQ_sld would halve lam_min and quarter the gain): (i) it is not cap-stable -- at L = 128, taper uv = 0.30, lam_min(M_*) = -3.211e-3, -3.134e-3, -7.887e-3, -3.477e-2, -1.050e-1 and lam_min/||M_*|| = -0.0122, -0.0067, -0.0105, -0.0352, -0.0753 for cap = 1e4, 1e6, 1e8, 1e10, 1e12, while theta is cap-stable to 4 digits (0.29117, 0.29119, 0.29116, 0.29118, 0.29119); (ii) the achievable gain collapses as the cap grows: rank-one gain/g_Q(dc) = 1.463e-4, 1.948e-6, 1.722e-10, 3.534e-11, 3.718e-12 on the same ladder (the violating directions have diverging curvature, g_Q(noise)/g_Q(dc) = 1.3e3 ... 5.5e13); the second taper uv = 0.20 repeats the pattern (lam_min/||M_*|| = -0.0125, -0.0070, -0.0088, -0.0258, -0.0287; gain = 5.808e-4 ... 6.444e-13) with theta shifted by 10% (0.2615); (iii) the mechanism: the circle model violates Moebius rigidity at O(1/L) (|dc_DD|/|dc| = 0.346, 0.214, 0.153, 0.101, 0.075 and |dc_AA|/|dc| = 0.048, 0.032, 0.024, 0.016, 0.012 at L = 64..256, both ~ 1/L, whereas the exact defect is purely A-D off-diagonal), and g_Q weights those spurious blocks by w up to the cap -- taken separately the blocks of delta_c carry g_Q of order 1e5 x g_Q(delta_c), so t_* and hence M_*, tau_* are contaminated exactly where the weights are largest.
WHAT MAY AND MAY NOT BE CONCLUDED. The numerics are consistent with the isometric orbit carrying the tangent optimum and kappa_opt = 1 - theta, and they exclude any O(1) gain from non-isometric or boundary-moving directions (every measured rank-one gain is <= 1.05e-3 g_Q(ddot): the largest, 1.049e-3 at h = 0.24, Ymax = 6, is reported only in F2_RESULTS.md:302-303; in the runs with output files it is <= 3.85e-4, f2_t4_h024.out l.6; all fall like h^1.85/Ymax^2). They do NOT establish that the optimal N_1, Y_1 vanish: Thm 4.4(d) delivers a global minimiser, not uniqueness, and the marginal case lam_min -> 0^- found here is precisely where uniqueness is not delivered.

cards.title: KKT sign criterion: when the isometric orbit carries the all-channel second-order optimum
cards.statement: PROVED (rigor/exact_optimum_tangent_problem.tex, Sec. 4). Let delta_* be the b-orthogonal residual of ddelta on the closure of the LINEAR class L = {[Q,G] : G bounded anti-self-adjoint, supported in D} (no minimiser is posited), t_* := SLD(delta_*) (S_Q(t_*) = delta_*, t_*~_ik = w_ik delta_*~_ik), tau_* := E_D t_* E_D and M_* := (1/2) E_D (t_* Q + Q t_*) E_D = Herm(t_{*,DA} Q_AD) + Herm(t_{*,DD} Q_DD) = Herm((t_* Q)_DD). Since w is unbounded, t_* need NOT be Hilbert-Schmidt: M_* and tau_* are quadratic FORMS, defined intrinsically by <psi,M_* psi> := 4 b(delta_*, A(0,|psi><psi|,0)) and <psi,tau_* psi> := -4 b(delta_*, A(0,0,|psi><psi|)) on the domain D of psi for which those directions lie in the form domain F (Def. def:forms); 'M_* >= 0' is a form inequality and lambda_min may be -inf. Normalisation (Lemma lem:norm): g_Q(delta) = (1/4) Tr(t_delta delta), V(t_delta) = 2 g_Q(delta), d g_Q(delta)[eta] = (1/2) Tr(t_delta eta) (S10 (C4) is internally inconsistent with its own S_Q(t) = delta; the ratio and all sign conditions are unaffected). (i) Lemma lem:deriv: the one-sided derivative along an admissible non-isometric direction A(0,N_1,Y_1) is (1/2)[Tr(N_1 M_*) - Tr(Y_1 tau_*)]; it vanishes along the linear class; along the admissible unbounded generator G = -lambda D_chi|_D it equals 2 lambda (1-theta) g_Q(ddelta) (>= 0; > 0 iff theta < 1). (ii) Thm. thm:kktmain: (a) M_* >= 0 and M_* - tau_* >= 0 <=> (c) Tr(N_1 M_*) >= Tr[(N_1^{1/2} tau_* N_1^{1/2})_+] for all bounded N_1 >= 0; (b) M_* >= (tau_*)_+ is sufficient but strictly stronger (the operator order is not a lattice); AMENDED after the referee report: (d) (zeta_*,0,0) is a GLOBAL minimiser of the tangent programme <=> (a) AND (e), where (e) E(zeta) := 2 b(delta_*, A(zeta,0,0)) >= 0 for every admissible isometry generator zeta with A(zeta,0,0) in F; (a) alone is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT, because the feasible cone also contains the one-sided boundary-moving isometry directions (unbounded generators). If (a) and (e) hold then T = (1-theta) g_Q(ddelta), i.e. kappa_opt = 1 - theta exactly, and under H1 and H2 (Thm. thm:value) E^(2) = (1-theta) f_2 z^2 (1+o(1)). If (a) fails, a violating psi gives a strictly better feasible datum (Cor. cor:better, eq:gain2); kappa_opt < 1 - theta needs one admissible psi with Delta < 0 AND finite g_Q(d_psi), so a violation that vanishes with the weight cap or the mesh is a regularisation artefact. (iii) Prop. prop:bdryfun: E MUST be evaluated on the blocks of A (A_AD = -Q_AD zeta, A_DD = -(zeta* Q_DD + Q_DD zeta)); the commutator form -2 b(delta_*,[Q,zeta]) of Lemma lem:commQ is valid only for BOUNDED anti-self-adjoint zeta (where E = 0) and deletes exactly the boundary term (2'). E is additive, positively homogeneous and vanishes on the closure of L; when the cyclicity Tr(t_*[Q,zeta]) = Tr([t_*,Q] zeta) is legitimate (zeta bounded, t_* trace class), E(zeta) = (1/2)Tr(E_D[Q,t_*]E_D zeta) = 0 by the stationarity Prop. prop:S: E is exactly the cyclicity anomaly, a pure BOUNDARY functional, equal to (1/2)Tr((-2 sigma_zeta) M_*) whenever -2 sigma_zeta lies in the form domain of M_*. In the modular frame D = {y>0} has two endpoints (y = 0, the junction with A; y = +inf, the moving endpoint x = 1), and modulo the closure of L the VECTOR-FIELD subcone of admissible generators is generated by zeta_0 = -E_D d/dy E_D (the shift semigroup g(y) -> g(y-a), i.e. x -> 1 - e^{-a}(1-x); moves the junction y = 0) and zeta_inf = -lambda D_chi|_D (further compression; moves y = +inf); for the whole admissible cone this is hypothesis H3. E(zeta_inf) = 2 lambda (1-theta) g_Q(ddelta) is proved, hence E(zeta_inf) >= 0; E(zeta_inf) > 0 is equivalent to theta < 1, which is NOT proved (rem:whytheta (i), :1461-1464; verdict gap :1504-1507). So, ON THE MODEL CONE {alpha zeta_0 + beta zeta_inf + closure of L : alpha, beta >= 0}, (e) is equivalent to the single inequality E(zeta_0) = 2 b(delta_*, A(zeta_0,0,0)) >= 0; the identity E(zeta_0) = (1/2) Tr((-2 sigma_{zeta_0}) M_*) would need -2 sigma_{zeta_0} = delta_0 (x) delta_0 in the form domain of M_*, which fails (delta_0 is not in h_D). HYPOTHESIS H3 (cone hypothesis, Def. hyp:H3, read in F): for every admissible isometry generator zeta with A(zeta,0,0) in F there are alpha, beta >= 0 and eta in the b-closure of the linear class with A(zeta,0,0) = alpha A(zeta_0,0,0) + beta A(zeta_inf,0,0) + eta. (No boundary-form reformulation: that would be strictly weaker, trivially true for zeta = i m(y), and would not imply (e).) The reduction to the two model directions is PROVED ONLY for generators of vector-field type; shift semigroups of multiplicity > 1 (Cooper-Wold) and unbounded skew-adjoint zeta = i m(y) with [Q, i m] outside the closure of L escape both arguments, and excluding them is exactly the content of H3. Under H3, if A(zeta_0,0,0) is not in F then alpha = 0 is forced and (e) holds OUTRIGHT, E(zeta) = beta E(zeta_inf) >= 0 (rem:H3space), the junction inequality never being invoked; that A(zeta_0,0,0) is not in F (E(zeta_0) = +inf, so (e) is vacuous at zeta_0 rather than satisfied with a margin) rests on F2's divergent corner term (rem:T5 (ii)), i.e. it is numerical. E(zeta_0) >= 0 remains the operative test for REGULARISED junction directions (finite mesh), which is what F2 T5 measures. (iv) Prop. prop:S: stationarity on the LINEAR class <=> E_D[Q,t_*]E_D = 0, i.e. (t_* Q)_DD = M_* self-adjoint: S10's condition (S) holds automatically at the new point. (v) Prop. prop:s10 (trace-class t; S10 Thm 3.2 and Prop 5.2), dictionary to S10 Thm 3.2: Sigma_2 -> (tQ)_DD is the loss-of-isometry (N_1) condition M >= 0; Sigma_1 = Sigma_2 - t_DD >= 0 is the NOISE (Y_1) condition M >= tau; Sigma_1 = Sigma_1* is the rotation condition. NUMERICAL, NOT PROVED HERE (recorded on kkt-noise-criterion-numerics, all-channel-optimum-value, theta-value and compression-not-second-order-minimiser): (a) holds in the limit, although every finite run fails it (F2 T4, rigid frame of Prop 6.2: lambda_min(M_*)/||M_*|| = -4.1e-3, -1.9e-3, -8.2e-4, -3.7e-4 at h = 0.24, 0.12, 0.06, 0.03; violation ~ h^1.15 and ~ 1/Ymax, rank-one gain ~ h^1.85); E(zeta_0) > 0 on the model cone (F2 T5: E(zeta_0)/g_Q(ddelta) = +34.1, +66.9, +131.3, +258.0 at h = 0.24, 0.12, 0.06, 0.03 for the admissible backward/dissipative scheme, a scheme-dependent total ~ h^-0.97 dominated by an upwind-viscosity term; centred = 0, the linear class; forward = inadmissible, negative; the continuum piece is the corner term (1/2) M_*(0,0)/h = +10.3, +16.1, +24.7, +37.2, ~ h^-0.60, so M_*(y,y) -> +inf as y -> 0+ and E(zeta_0) = +inf: the junction direction is infinitely penalised at first order); E(zeta_inf) reproduces 2(1-theta_h) g_Q(ddelta) to 1e-15, and the A-form and boundary-form expressions agree to 2e-10 ... 2e-8; the commutator form returns, even for zeta_inf, -9.1e-6, +1.9e-4, -9.9e-3, +7.4e-2 at h = 0.24, 0.12, 0.06, 0.03 and -63, -1.6e6 on other rungs of the scan (O(1), no information on the true 2 lambda (1-theta) g_Q(ddelta) = 1.26-1.37 g_Q(ddelta); prop:bdryfun (2')); theta = 0.384 +- 0.003, hence kappa_opt = 1 - theta = 0.616 +- 0.003 conditional on H1, H2 AND H3 and on the mesh-verified (a) and (e); and (S) FAILS at the compression, i.e. E_D u E_D != 0 (||E_D u E_D||_2^2/||u||_2^2 = 0.0143, S10 cor:maximal eq:thetalb).

cards.statement: (a) Bounded generators (thm:exact, rigor/kubo_mori_second_variation.tex:215): for A = A* in M (bounded), u_s = e^{isA}, omega_s = omega o Ad u_s: D(omega || omega_s) = || h(Delta)^{1/2} (u_s - 1) Omega ||^2 in [0, infinity], h(lambda) = lambda - 1 - log lambda, with the sum rule int (lambda - 1) d nu_s = 0 along the orbit; liminf s^{-2} D >= g_KM/2 with no further hypothesis (thm:lower), g_KM = -2 <A Omega, log Delta A Omega> (lem:kms); D = (s^2/2) g_KM + o(s^2) under (U_eps) (thm:main), which holds in particular when A is modularly analytic in a strip, (A_eps) => (U_eps) (lem:AtoU). cards.title: Longo-Xu Remark 4.3: adjacent-interval CMI (c/6) log(1+z) for every rational conformal net (conjecture)
cards.statement: Conjecture (Longo-Xu, Remark 4.3): for every rational conformal net of central charge c, the vacuum conditional mutual information of adjacent intervals A = (-a,0), B = (0,b), C = (b,b+l) is I(A:C|B) = (c/6) log[(a+b)(b+l)/(b(a+b+l))] = (c/6) log(1+z). Proved only for the free fermion net A_r (c = r), its finite-index subnets and the finite-index extensions of Longo-Xu (card longo-xu-cmi); the project states that the general claim is not proved and does not use it (adjacent_interval_cmi_longo_xu.tex scope box l. 327-330; paper1 rem:LX-scope).

cards.title: Longo-Xu CMI of adjacent intervals for the free fermion net A_r, its finite-index subnets and extensions
cards.statement: Let the chiral net be the free fermion net A_r (central charge c = r), a finite-index subnet of it, or one of the finite-index extensions treated after Longo-Xu Thm 4.2, and assume strong additivity. For adjacent intervals A = (-a,0), B = (0,b), C = (b,b+c) (here c is the length of C) in the vacuum, the conditional mutual information (Longo-Xu generalized mutual information, equivalently the gap limit) is finite and I(A:C|B) = (r/6) log[(a+b)(b+c)/(b(a+b+c))] = (r/6) log(1+z) = -(r/6) log eta (adjacent_interval_cmi_longo_xu.tex eq:abc-formula; Note 2 eq:longoxu-limit; paper 1 thm:LX). Read as the quantum-Markov defect of the chain A-B-C; the Petz recovery error is the natural quantitative companion. Scope (Note 1 scope box, l. 327-330; paper 1 rem:LX-scope): the rigorous conclusion covers only this free-fermion class; the formula with r replaced by the central charge for every rational conformal net is Longo-Xu's Remark 4.3, a conjecture (card longo-xu-cmi-general-c), and a full 2D CFT needs a separate left-right analysis.

cards.title: Moebius reduction: the fidelity and relative entropy of the geometric recovery depend on (a, L, s) only through zeta = a s/(a+L), including the half-line chart a = infinity (zeta = s) (Note 5 Lemma 1.1; check_note5_theory prop:closed)
cards.statement: For the chiral free fermion, F(omega, omega o gamma_s) and the relative entropy of the geometrically recovered state depend on (a, L, s) only through zeta = a s/(a+L), where 1 + zeta is the cross ratio of the four points -a < 0 < L/(1+s) < L; the proof uses only Moebius covariance of the vacuum (the half-density action commutes with the Hardy projection and carries F(X) onto F(g(X))). Note 5's proof (lem:mobius) assumes g(I) bounded (fidelity_recovered_quasifree.tex:208; check_note5_theory.tex:180-185), so it covers finite configurations only. The reduction to the half-line chart a = infinity, L = 1 (zeta = s), used by uhlmann_upper_bound.tex:69-71, :923-926 (the Moebius map with its pole at -a), follows from the closed-form proof of check_note5_theory.tex prop:closed (Prop. 6.1). In the xi-representation the defect kernel is zeta S_p S_p' / (sinh M (sinh M + 2 zeta S_p S_p')), with zeta = s beta_0/L = a s/(a+L), a function of zeta alone, and that proof holds unchanged at a = infinity.

cards.title: Second-order network law: Phi_tot = sum zeta_j zeta_k G(y_j - y_k), G = c Ghat universal
cards.statement: For corners at modular positions y_k with strengths zeta_k (frame of the whole chain), -log F(omega, omega o beta_Phi) = sum_{j,k} zeta_j zeta_k G(y_j - y_k) + o(|zeta|^2) with G(Delta) = c Ghat(Delta), Ghat(0) = 1/(12 pi^2) (Theorem A), Ghat even and positive-definite as the Fourier transform of the positive spectral density of the first-order corner defect in the modular frame (positive-definiteness does NOT imply Ghat >= 0 pointwise; the sign for Delta > 0 is open, card corner-correlation-kernel). The remainder must be shown UNIFORM in the corner separations for the applications in which zeta -> 0 and Delta -> inf together (vwz-protocol-ordering). Lower bound: data processing + Legendre form, linear in the defect. Upper bound: Uhlmann + C^{1,1} flow extension with finitely many second-derivative jumps; expected global bound Phi_tot <= -(1/2) log(1 - 2 sum zeta zeta G). Separation constraint: admissible protocols ALL of whose corners are weak (zeta_j <= eps for every j) cannot have two of them close at distinct points -- for the L->R Petz chain (e^{Delta_k} - 1) zeta_k^(I) = 2 r_k (1+v_k)/(1+r_k) >= 2 r_k/(1+r_k) exactly, and zeta_j <= eps for all j forces e^{Delta_k} >= 2/eps, PROVED in rigor/network_corner_calculus.tex Thm 11.1 (track G1a; REF-P6-3: stands; sharp as eps -> 0, exact minima 20.0499, 66.6817, 200.0050, 666.6682 at eps = 0.1, 0.03, 0.01, 0.003, rigor/ref_p6_3_separation.out; 1/eps for general admissible s_k >= lambda_k; card corner-separation-constraint); with only the pair weak the separation can stay O(1). Hence, for all-weak L->R chains and given the uniform remainder, at strict second order Phi_tot = f2 sum_points (sum_steps zeta)^2 + O(eps^2 sup_{Delta >= log(2/eps)} |Ghat(Delta)|): coherent addition at a common junction, additivity in zeta^2 across distinct junctions. Universality of Ghat by the H_T argument of Theorem B.

cards.title: The Petz map is not second-order optimal (compression 4x better at leading order)
cards.statement: Per chirality (Prop. prop:convex(4), rigor/optimality_second_order.tex): the zero-collar geometric compression (s = lambda) is an admissible recovery channel with -log F = Phi(z) = f2 z^2 (1+o(1)), f2 = c/(12 pi^2) (Theorem A, card const-f2), and Phi obeys the proved one-sided bound Phi(zeta) <= -(1/2) log(1 - 2 f2 zeta^2) = f2 zeta^2 (1 + f2 zeta^2 + O(zeta^4)) (free fermion, for 2 f2 zeta^2 < 1; rigor/rate_of_remainder.tex thm:global with sec:rrr-f2; card rate-of-remainder), whereas the ordinary Petz map (s = 2 lambda, zeta = 2z) gives Phi(2z) = 4 f2 z^2 (1+o(1)): at leading order the Petz map is worse by the factor 4. Phi is nondecreasing (check_note5_theory.tex prop:mono), so within the geometric family the infimum is attained at the compression, and the range constraint beta(A(BC)) subset A(B) (s >= lambda, i.e. zeta >= z) is active there (Remark rem:active). NOT proved: a two-sided O(z^3) remainder. S8 writes f2 z^2 + O(z^3) and 4 f2 z^2 + O(z^3), but the cited step gives only the leading order, and every lower bound with a rate, e.g. Phi >= f2 zeta^2 (1 - 0.99 zeta + O(zeta^2)), is conditional on a cutoff-uniform remainder (Problem 7.2 of quadratic_limit.tex; rate_of_remainder.tex:772-775 and the status table :795-798). The 2D clause of prop:convex(4) (spatial compression 2 f2 z^2 against Petz 8 f2 z^2, both chiralities) is stated in the proposition (:95-97) but no proof step addresses it; it needs the factorisation into two chiral halves, proved only for the massless Dirac fermion (check_note5_theory.tex prop:chirality; card two-chirality-law), and is not claimed here. (14), :636; card optimal-channel-structure).

cards.title: Zero-collar Petz map of the free fermion is a geometric compression
cards.statement: For the r-component free chiral fermion with I = ABC = (-a, L), A = (-a, 0), D = BC = (0, L), B = (0, b) and lambda = c/b (c the length of C): for every s >= lambda the glued map k_s = id on A, h_s(x) = Lx/(L + sx) on D (C^{1,1}, joined with one derivative at 0) maps I onto J_s = (-a, L/(1+s)) inside AB, and the induced CAR isomorphism beta_s(a(f)) = a(W_{k_s} f) extends uniquely to a normal *-isomorphism beta-bar_s: F_r(I) -> F_r(J_s) (continuum_petz_free_fermion.tex thm:normal-extension; rigor/check_note4.tex thm:normal); Note 4 obtains the extension by quasi-equivalence (Powers-Stormer-Araki, from the trace-class defect), not from a unitary implementer. For s = s_t = lambda (1 + e^{-2 pi t}) its restriction to every positive-collar algebra is the FHSW rotated Petz map (eq:restriction-normal-beta); the ordinary Petz map is s = 2 lambda (t = 0), and the zero-collar geometric compression is s = lambda (t -> +infinity), whose range is F_r(J_lambda) = F_r(AB), the D-part landing exactly on D_lambda = B. Implementer: beta-bar_s = Ad Gamma(W~_s) on F_r(I), where W~_s is the one-particle unitary of the C^{1,1} extension k~_s of k_s to the whole line (card c11-extension-implementer: rigor/uhlmann_upper_bound.tex def:ext, cor:implementer, prop:vector); W_{k_s} itself maps H_I onto H_{J_s} and is not a unitary of the full one-particle space, so Gamma(W_{k_s}) is not defined. Trace norms (continuum_petz_free_fermion.tex thm:trace-norm), zeta = as/(a+L): the scalar endpoint kernel R_s (taken without the factor i/(2 pi)) has ||R_s||_1 = (1/2) log(1 + zeta); the off-diagonal symbol block has ||Delta_s||_1 = (r/(4 pi)) log(1 + zeta); the symbol defect is ||Q_I - Q~_s||_1 = (r/(2 pi)) log(1 + zeta).

cards.title: Phase 6 plan: multi-interval networks as a corner calculus
cards.statement: Sequential one-sided zero-collar recovery along a chain A_1...A_n is treated as a composition of parabolic Moebius compressions. Exact and verified: zeta = kappa beta_I(p) is the coefficient of the universal field w(y) = -4 sinh^2(y/2) 1_{y>0}, Theorem A's zeta = as/(a+L) being the one-corner case. Remaining tracks (not launched): G1b second-order network law Phi = sum zeta_j zeta_k G(y_j - y_k) with the universal positive-definite kernel G = c Ghat, Ghat(0) = 1/(12 pi^2), remainder uniform in the separations; G2 lattice sequential Gaussian Petz maps (VWZ Protocols 1(A), 1(B), 2, 3; Phi(1):Phi(3) = Phi_A(a/b):Phi_A(2a/b) exactly, conditional Phi(2) -> 2 Phi(1)); G3 Ghat(Delta) in two independent discretisations plus exact two-corner fidelities (VWZ Fig. 25 carries no information on Ghat).
