cards.title: Phi' is NOT nondecreasing on (0, infinity): the step used in prop:chirality <1>8 is false
cards.statement: REFUTED. Claim (rigor/check_note5_theory.tex prop:chirality, step <1>8, l. 1413-1418): the single-chirality zero-collar recovery error Phi(zeta) = -log F(omega, omega-tilde_zeta) of the free chiral fermion has a nondecreasing derivative on the whole half-line zeta > 0. It is false. (1) The FHSW bound in the continuum (rigor/check_note4.tex prop:limit: FHSW Thm 1 plus the collar limit; also fidelity_recovered_quasifree.tex:473) gives int p(t) [-log F(omega, omega-tilde_t)] dt <= (1/2) I(A:C|B) = (r/12) log(1+z), with p(t) = pi/(1 + cosh 2 pi t) even and of total mass 1, and I(A:C|B) = (r/6) log(1+z) (card longo-xu-cmi). (2) By the single-chirality collapse (card two-chirality-law) -log F(omega, omega-tilde_t) = Phi(z(1 + e^{-2 pi t})), whose argument is >= 2z for t <= 0; Phi >= 0 is nondecreasing (card phi-monotone-in-zeta). Hence (1/2) Phi(2z) <= int_{t<=0} p(t) Phi(zeta_t) dt <= (r/12) log(1+z), i.e. Phi(zeta) <= (r/6) log(1 + zeta/2) for all zeta > 0: Phi grows at most logarithmically. (3) If Phi' were nondecreasing, Phi would be convex; Phi is not identically 0 and Phi(0+) = 0 (Theorem A: Phi ~ f2 zeta^2), so Phi'(zeta_1) > 0 for some zeta_1 (otherwise Phi would be nonincreasing, hence identically 0), and convexity gives Phi(zeta) >= Phi(zeta_1) + Phi'(zeta_1)(zeta - zeta_1), linear growth, contradicting (2). Numerically (card large-zeta-values; numerics/results_largezeta_certified.txt, r = 1): Phi(zeta)/zeta = 5.25e-3, 4.66e-3, 3.76e-3 at zeta = 4.27, 8.53, 17.1 decreases, whereas a convex Phi with Phi(0+) = 0 has Phi/zeta nondecreasing; even with the rigorous lower bound Phi(4.267) >= 2.187e-2, convexity would force Phi(8.533) >= 4.374e-2, above every extrapolated estimate (at most 4.306e-2). The document's justification (prop:mono plus convexity at small zeta) does not imply the claim. Consequence: the minimum at lambda = 0 of the two-chirality law is unproved (card two-chirality-minimum-at-lambda-zero). The weaker property 'zeta Phi'(zeta) nondecreasing', which would suffice there, is consistent with the logarithmic bound and with the certified values, but is unproved.

cards.title: Corner data of all one-sided protocols for n = 4 and n = 5: the holonomy is the starting block
cards.statement: For a complete one-sided protocol with SINGLE-interval conditioning, starting block J_0 = A_i..A_j (j >= i+1) and common rotation parameter t (theta_t = (1+e^{-2 pi t})/2, theta_0 = 1 the ordinary Petz value), hypothesis (H) holds and the corner measure is kappa = sum_{k<i} sigma^L_k delta_{p_{k+2}} + sum_{k>j} sigma^R_k delta_{p_{k-1}} with sigma^L_k = theta_t 2 l_k/(l_{k+1}(l_k+l_{k+1})) and sigma^R_k = theta_t 2 l_k/(l_{k-1}(l_{k-1}+l_k)) -- INDEPENDENT of the order of the steps. Hence all binom((i-1)+(n-j), i-1) orders for a given starting block give the same recovered state, the 2^{n-2} protocols with a starting PAIR fall into exactly n-1 classes (one per pair), the left corners occupy p_3..p_{i+1} and the right corners p_j..p_{n-1}, and they overlap in exactly one point (a double corner at p_{i+1} = p_j) iff j = i+1. n = 4 (4 protocols, 3 classes): start A_1A_2 (RR) -> {p_2: sigma^R_3, p_3: sigma^R_4} = VWZ Protocol 2; start A_2A_3 (LR and RL, identical) -> {p_3: sigma^L_1 + sigma^R_4} = VWZ Protocol 3; start A_3A_4 (LL) -> {p_3: sigma^L_1, p_4: sigma^L_2}. Equal lengths l = (1,1,1,1): zeta^(I) = (0.75 at p_2, 1 at p_3), (2 at p_3), (1 at p_3, 0.75 at p_4). n = 5 (8 protocols, 4 classes): start A_1A_2 (RRR) -> p_2,p_3,p_4 simple; start A_2A_3 (LRR, RLR, RRL) -> double corner at p_3 plus p_4; start A_3A_4 (LLR, LRL, RLL) -> p_3 plus double corner at p_4; start A_4A_5 (LLL) -> p_3,p_4,p_5 simple. Union-conditioning variants for n = 4: VWZ 1(A) (one corner at p_2) and 1(B) (two corners at p_2, same measure by the identity 2c/(b(b+c)) + 2d/((b+c)(b+c+d)) = 2(c+d)/(b(b+c+d))) satisfy (H); the variant 'add D on C, then A on BC' does NOT (REF-P6-0's counterexample geometry: the mass is displaced off the junction).

cards.title: Exact root fidelity of two quasi-free CAR states from their symbols (Note 5 Thm. 2.1)
cards.statement: For two gauge-invariant quasi-free states on a FINITE-DIMENSIONAL one-particle space h with symbols Q1, Q2 (0 < Q < 1), G = Q/(1-Q): -log F = (1/2) sum log(1+t) + (1/2) sum log(1+s) - sum log(1 + sqrt(tau)), t = eig G1, s = eig G2, tau = eig(G1^{1/2} G2 G1^{1/2}) (Note 5 Thm. 2.1, thm:finite-fidelity); equivalently F = det(1-Q1)^{1/2} det(1-Q2)^{1/2} prod_i (1 + sigma_i(C)), C = (1-Q1)^{-1/2} Q1^{1/2} Q2^{1/2} (1-Q2)^{-1/2}, the form that is numerically stable when eigenvalues sit near 0 and 1. For infinite-dimensional h the formula is obtained as the monotone limit over finite-dimensional compressions (Note 5, Thm det-rep) when the two states are quasi-equivalent. Implemented in mpmath at dps 60-80 and validated against the brute-force many-body fidelity on three random modes to 12 digits.
cards.verify: Note 5 Thm. 2.1; numerics/optimality/petz_ref.py (mpmath, 60-90 digits); selftest() in numerics/optimality_all/exact_fidelity_rotated.py.

cards.title: Second-order problem over quasi-free channels is a convex SDP
cards.statement: Gauge-invariant quasi-free channels have data (X,Y), CP iff Y >= 0 and XX* + Y <= 1; in the variables (X, Z = X Q_BB X* + Y) the feasible set F = {X Q_BB X* <= Z <= 1 - X(1-Q_BB)X*} is convex and semidefinite representable, the recovered symbol is affine, and the SLD form g_Q is a convex quadratic; every local minimum is global. Caveat: g_Q is the second-order term only for defects small relative to e^{-kappa_max} (order of limits); cap weights, never drop modes.

cards.title: Second-order (SLD / quantum Fisher) expansion of the quasi-free root fidelity in finite dimensions (Note 5 Prop. 2.3)
cards.statement: For gauge-invariant quasi-free states on a finite-dimensional one-particle space with symbols Q and Q + eps D (0 < Q < 1, D = D^*), -log F(omega_Q, omega_{Q+eps D}) = (eps^2/4) sum_{i,k} |D_ik|^2 / (q_i(1-q_k) + q_k(1-q_i)) + O(eps^3) in an eigenbasis of Q, with weight 1 + cosh((kappa_i+kappa_k)/2)/cosh((kappa_i-kappa_k)/2) in the modular variables q = (1+e^kappa)^{-1}, and the analogous Kubo-Mori expansion of the relative entropy.

cards.title: Remainder of Theorem A: global upper bound Phi <= -(1/2) log(1 - 2 f2 zeta^2); c3 <= 0 as a limsup; no positive log^-2 term
cards.statement: For the zero-collar compression of the free chiral fermion (f2 = g_B/8 = 1/(12 pi^2) per component): (1) group bound (lem:groupbound): for U_s = e^{sK} with [P_-, K] Hilbert-Schmidt, ||V_s||_2^2 <= s^2 ||P_- K P_+||_2^2 exactly, V_s = P_- U_s P_+; (2) global bound (thm:global with prop:rrr, unconditional): for K = D + i h' with h' in the admissible commutant class, Gamma(U_s)^* Omega represents the recovered state and Phi(zeta) <= -(1/2) log(1 - 2 f2^K zeta^2) with inf over h' of f2^K = g_B/8 = f2, hence Phi(zeta) <= -(1/2) log(1 - 2 f2 zeta^2) = f2 zeta^2 (1 + f2 zeta^2 + O(zeta^4)) for zeta < (2 f2)^{-1/2}, with no cubic term; (3) consequences (cor:c3sign): limsup_{zeta -> 0} (Phi - f2 zeta^2)/zeta^3 <= 0, so c3 <= 0 IF Phi = f2 zeta^2 (1 + c3 zeta + o(zeta)); and there is no remainder + b zeta^2/log^2(1/zeta) with b > 0, since Phi - f2 zeta^2 <= f2^2 zeta^4/(1 - 2 f2 zeta^2); this refutes the zeta^2 log^-2 remainder of Note 5 Cor. 4.2 (a double count). NOT claimed here: that Phi has an expansion in integer powers, and the values c3 = -0.99(1), c4 = +0.9(1) (card remainder-c3-c4-values, heuristic); every lower bound with a rate is conditional on a cutoff-uniform constant (summary table, l. 786-800).

cards.title: Two git repositories over one work tree: public project, private third-party material
cards.statement: Since 2026-09-20 the cft_cmi directory is covered by two git repositories sharing one work tree, so no file moved and no tool was reconfigured. .git holds the publishable project: papers, notes, rigor documents, numerics scripts and the 97 tracked .out files, 83 under numerics/ and 14 under rigor/, 96 of them run captures and one (rigor/_probe.out) a stray LaTeX bookmark file, of which 23 are named by a card's evidence token (./pgit (held privately) check prints the file count of each repository, and both move with every commit, so neither of those two counts is fixed here), remote https://github.com/alexander-stottmeister/cft-cmi; .git-private holds what must not be published (235 files on 2026-09-23, and it moves on every private commit -- a new page excerpt, a new source PDF, or a note held here rather than published, as one was while the plan-page exposure was open: the 178 page excerpts in rigor/shots (held privately), the 47 source PDFs in refs, the five cited-result compendia rigor/cited_R1..R4.tex and cited_results_all.tex, plan_page/petz_program_plan.html (held privately), CHECKLIST.md (held privately), PRIVATE.md (held privately), pgit and pgit-exclude (held privately), which is exactly what git --git-dir=.git-private ls-files lists outside the first two directories), remote https://github.com/alexander-stottmeister/cft-cmi-private, driven by the wrapper ./pgit (status, sync, check, push). The companion remote has been private since 2026-09-20 and must stay so; the project remote was private from its recreation on 2026-09-21 until 2026-09-22, when it was made public and the site went live. The two tracked sets are disjoint (overlap 0) and the files tracked by neither are regenerable build products and caches (436 files, 201.6 MB on 2026-09-23; the knowledge base writes one review packet per review into rigor/ and they are tracked by neither, so this count rises by one per review). Three things make it work: (1) rigor_preamble.tex defines \\shot[width]{file} and \\shotc, an exact drop-in for \\includegraphics that embeds the excerpt when rigor/shots is present and prints a framed locator note when absent -- 255 call sites in 19 documents were converted, local builds are unchanged (network_corner_calculus 42 pp with images) and a clone of the REMOTE builds with one placeholder per call site (quadratic_limit 26 pp / 0 images against 27 pp / 8 locally, verified by REF-INFRA-2); (2) the 24 python scripts that hardcoded /Users/alex now resolve paths against a computed _ROOT (37 literals), and the four shell scripts that hardcoded a session scratchpad interpreter now honour $PYTHON; (3) because a work-tree .gitignore outranks info/exclude, the private repo cannot see NEW files under its own paths, so ./pgit sync force-stages them and ./pgit check fails on either an overlap or untracked excerpts; since a bare clone carries no info/exclude, the whitelist is tracked as pgit-exclude and ./pgit reinstalls it on every run. The public history never contained an excerpt or a source PDF (verified against a clone of the remote). It DID contain the five cited-result compendia, and a history rewrite was needed and carried out on 2026-09-21: they were removed from every commit and force-pushed, and no ref of the remote reaches them any more (verified from a fresh mirror clone: 0 objects bear their names, the tag's tree is clean, none of the paths it ever added is an excerpt or a PDF). THEY REMAINED RECOVERABLE FROM THE REMOTE UNTIL 2026-09-21, AND ARE NOT NOW. The rewrite bought unreachability, not deletion: GitHub retains unreachable objects and serves them by SHA, and three independent REST routes each returned the files, the largest of them byte-identical to the private copy at its full 299,915 bytes. The seeds were not confidential either. The repository's Actions, events and activity endpoints and the owner's timeline published 44 discarded commits between them, the activity feed labelled the force-push and named the discarded head outright, each run published a root tree id that reached the files in two calls with no commit hash at all, and one seed walked the whole discarded history. Seven public-tracked files in this repository gave the route in words. cards.title: Markov c-function along the massive flow
cards.statement: For the massive (staggered-mass) Dirac chain, c_M(R) := 3R^2 I_{R-2}(2)/4 and c_E(R) := 3R (S(R+2) - S(R-2))/4 satisfy c_M >= c_E at every computed point, and along the flow (mu R from 0 to infinity, mu = m/2) both fall monotonically from c = 1 towards 0 (dc_E/dR < 0 and dc_M/dR < 0 at every point with m > 0; numerics/lattice/petz_thermal_rg.out l. 393-549). The ratio c_M/c_E behaves like m R only in a scaling window (correlation length xi = 2/m >> 1 site and mu R >> 1; the free-field prediction from S(R) - S(infinity) ~ A e^{-2 mu R}); on the lattice at fixed m the ratio (c_M/c_E)/(mR) does not tend to 1: for m = 0.4 it is 1.196, 1.077, 1.020, 1.003, 0.992, 0.972 at R = 6, 10, 16, 20, 24, 40 and still falling, and at R = 40 it is 0.825 for m = 0.8 and 0.563 for m = 1.6 (plateaus f(0.8) ~ 0.83, f(1.6) ~ 0.56), while for small m (0.05, 0.1, 0.2) it is still above 1 and decreasing at R = 40 (1.36, 1.15, 1.05). This is consistent with c_M/c_E ~ m R in the continuum scaling limit (m -> 0 at fixed mu R >> 1), which the data do not reach; rigor/thermal_rg_gap_summary.md:73 quotes only R <= 16 at m = 0.4.

cards.title: Type-III second-variation lemma (fidelity half), under the vector hypothesis (V)
cards.statement: Let M be a von Neumann algebra with a cyclic and separating vector Omega, omega = <Omega, . Omega>, and let omega_s = <xi_s, . xi_s>|M be vector states given by unit vectors xi_s with xi_0 = Omega that are norm-differentiable at s = 0 (hypothesis (V), rigor/lemma_second_variation.tex l. 119-121), with tangent representative a = i xi'_0; the model case is xi_s = e^{-isA} Omega with A = A* on H, Omega in D(A), a = A Omega. Then F(omega, omega_s) = 1 - (s^2/8) g_B + o(s^2) and -log F(omega, omega_s) = (s^2/8) g_B + o(s^2), with g_B = g_B(a) given by the three faces (thm:three; card bures-three-faces) (thm:main). Without (V) the conclusion is not available: norm-differentiability of s -> omega_s in M_* does not imply (V) (Powers-Stormer gives only Holder exponent 1/2), and then only F = 1 - O(s) follows (Gap 5, l. 1345-1355). The Kubo-Mori half is only available on unitary orbits of generators affiliated with M (card km-exact-identity).

cards.title: Type-III sequential recovery bound: Bures distances add along a chain of von Neumann inclusions (chordal and second-order forms, no Hypothesis (U))
cards.statement: Let omega be a normal state on a von Neumann algebra M, N_1 subset N_2 subset ... subset N_m subset M von Neumann subalgebras with the same unit, R_k: N_{k+1} -> N_k normal unital 2-positive (Heisenberg-picture) recovery maps, R = R_1 o ... o R_{m-1}. CHORDAL FORM (Thm 12.6, thm:w6chord), no Hypothesis (U): with d_B = sqrt(2 - 2F), d_B(omega|N_m, omega|N_1 o R) <= sum_k d_B(omega|N_{k+1}, omega|N_k o R_k). Proof: telescoping through the states mu_j = omega|N_{m-j} o R_{m-j} o S_j, S_j = R_{m-j+1} o ... o R_{m-1} (steps <1>1-<1>3 of Thm 12.5, which do not use (U)), monotonicity of F under the channel S_j (Lemma 12.3, from Choi's inequality T(a^{-1}) >= T(a)^{-1} for unital 2-positive T, Lemma 12.2, via the Schur complement, and Alberti-Uhlmann 2002 Thm 2(1), p. 6, and Cor 2(5), p. 8), and the triangle inequality of d_B (Alberti-Uhlmann 2002 Prop. 1(1), p. 3, stated there without proof and attributed to Bures 1969, which is NOT OBTAINED). SECOND-ORDER FORM (Cor 12.7(2), cor:w6-second), no (U): with Phi_tot = -log F(omega|N_m, omega|N_1 o R) and Phi_k = -log F(omega|N_{k+1}, omega|N_k o R_k), Phi_tot <= (sum_k sqrt(Phi_k))^2 (1 + o(1)) as all Phi_k -> 0; if each step extends to a normal unital 2-positive map on F(I) with error check-Phi_k, then Phi_k <= check-Phi_k and the same bound holds with check-Phi_k. SATURATION, 'if' direction only (Rem 12.8, rem:w6-sat): when all corners of the protocol coincide at one point (e.g. VWZ 1(B), Protocol 3), Thm 8.5 (thm:prot3, card corner-calculus) and Theorem A give Phi_tot = Phi_A(sum_k zeta_k) = f2 (sum_k zeta_k)^2 + o and check-Phi_k = f2 zeta_k^2 + o, so the second-order bound is saturated at second order. NOT claimed: the converse (non-saturation for corners at distinct points); the document compares with the conjectural network law W2 only 'as a target, not used' (l. 1962), and W2 would at best concern the extended errors check-Phi_k. NOT claimed: the ANGLE FORM (arccos F adds along the chain; Thm 12.5, thm:w6) and its exact form Phi_tot <= -log cos(sum_k arccos e^{-Phi_k}) (Cor 12.7(1), eq:w6-master). The document proves them only under Hypothesis (U), which is refuted (card hypothesis-u-natural-cone-fidelity), so they are vacuous as proved; the conditional statement is card sequential-recovery-angle-form-under-u. The angle inequality is expected to hold without (U), but no project document proves it and no card uses it.

cards.title: Exact single-observable fidelity bound (Alberti-Uhlmann) and its reduction to the recovered symbol
cards.statement: Lemma lem:single (rigor/optimality_all_channels.tex, Lemma 2.2): let phi, psi be normal states on a von Neumann algebra M, T = T* in M, m := phi(T), Delta := phi(T) - psi(T), N := ||T - m||. For every 0 < eps < 1/N, F(phi,psi) <= 1 - (eps/2) Delta + (eps^2/2) psi((T-m)^2)/(1 - eps N); hence, for every V' >= psi((T-m)^2) with 0 < Delta N < 2V', -log F(phi,psi) >= 1 - F(phi,psi) >= Delta^2/(8V') (1 - Delta N/V'). Prop. prop:red (Prop. 2.5): for a recovery channel beta with -log F(omega, omega^beta) <= E and a finite-rank self-adjoint t on h_I, T = dGamma(t), delta^beta = Q - Q^beta, V(t) = Tr(tQt(1-Q)): if Delta := Tr t delta^beta > 0 and V' := V(t) + 2 sqrt(2E) ||t||_1^2 > Delta ||t||_1/2, then -log F(omega, omega^beta) >= Delta^2/(8V') (1 - Delta ||t||_1/V') >= (Tr t delta^beta)^2/(8(V(t) + 2 sqrt(2E) ||t||_1^2)) (1 - |Tr t delta^beta| ||t||_1/V(t)), a bound that depends on beta only through the recovered symbol. These are lower bounds; they say nothing about the upper half. Not claimed here: 'for EVERY recovery channel -log F >= g_Q(Q - Q^beta)(1 - o(1)) in Legendre form' is Remark rem:use (2.6, :146-157), not a proof: it needs a near-maximising test operator with V(t) and ||t||_1 of order one, while the Legendre maximiser (the SLD) need not be finite rank, or even Hilbert-Schmidt in the continuum. The every-channel bound that is proved is Thm. thm:main(2) (card all-channel-equals-quasi-free, which uses this card): E_rec >= D_z (1 - o(1)), D_z = sup_t Delta_z(t)_+^2/(8V(t)), along any family of finite-rank t_z with ||t_z||_1^2/V(t_z) bounded and Delta_z(t_z) ||t_z||_1/V(t_z) -> 0, in particular liminf z^-2 E_rec >= sup over such families of liminf z^-2 Delta_z(t_z)^2/(8V(t_z)) (eq:liminf); by thm:main(3) the remainder control is automatic for finite-dimensional h_I.

cards.title: Hypothesis H1 of the tangent problem: g_Q-differentiability along the scaled family
cards.statement: For the first-order datum (zeta, N_1, Y_1) under consideration, the exact defect delta(s) of the scaled feasible family satisfies g_Q(delta(s) - s delta^(1)) = o(s^2) as s -> 0; this is known for the isometric orbit (S10 Lemma 6.1) and for finite-rank N_1, Y_1 with range in a modular window, and is a hypothesis in general because the g_Q-norm is strictly stronger than the Hilbert-Schmidt norm.
cards.verify: rigor/exact_optimum_tangent_problem.tex Def. 3.7 (hyp:H1) and Remark 3.8 (rem:H1), :417-431: known for the isometric orbit (S10 Lemma 6.1 <1>3-<1>4, numerically S10 Sec. 7(d) to 1e-3) and for finite-rank N_1, Y_1 with range in a modular window, a hypothesis in general; used by Thm. 3.9 (thm:upper, :433-456, minimising-sequence clause :439-441) and Thm. 3.17 (thm:value); status in Sec. 7, Conditional item 1 (:1601-1606: it fails for the inadmissible contraction family of Rem. 4.8) and To be supplied (:1628-1636).

cards.title: Hypothesis H2 of the tangent problem: localisation of the minimisers of the second-order programme
cards.statement: There are C < infinity and s_0 > 0 such that for 0 < s < s_0 the programme min_F g_Q(Q - Q_rec) has a minimiser (X_s, Z_s) of the scaled-family form for a first-order datum (zeta^(s), N_1^(s), Y_1^(s)) with ||N_1^(s)|| + ||Y_1^(s)|| <= C and g_Q(delta(s) - s delta^(1),(s)) = o(s^2) uniformly in s; the document calls it 'the lower bound in disguise' and does not prove it.
cards.verify: rigor/exact_optimum_tangent_problem.tex Def. 3.16 (hyp:H2) and the 'lower bound in disguise' paragraph (:625-635); Prop. 3.14 (prop:coerc) and Remark 3.15 (rem:noloc, :595-623) for why coercivity does not localise the minimiser; Thm. 3.17 (thm:value, :637-655) for its use; Remark 3.18 (rem:dual, eq:weakdual, :657-671) for the unconditional route; Sec. 7, Conditional item 2 (:1607-1613).
cards.next: Either prove H2 (localisation of the minimisers of min_F g_Q in the scaled-family form with ||N_1|| + ||Y_1|| <= C and a uniform o(s^2) remainder, overcoming Rem. rem:noloc: Q_AB has 0 in its essential spectrum), or bypass it by a finite-s dual certificate: one self-adjoint trace-class t (t_* at finite s) with Delta_z(t) >= 0 whose multipliers satisfy the sign conditions of S10 Thm. 3.2 at the optimal point, which gives the lower bound min_F g_Q >= Delta_z(t)^2/(8V(t)) through the weak-duality bound eq:weakdual (Rem. rem:dual, rigor/exact_optimum_tangent_problem.tex:657-671; To be supplied :1628-1636).

cards.title: Hypothesis H3 of the tangent problem (cone hypothesis): every admissible isometry generator with a feasible first-order datum lies in the model cone modulo the linear class
cards.statement: For every admissible isometry generator zeta with A(zeta,0,0) in the form domain F there are alpha, beta >= 0 and eta in the b-closure of the linear class L with A(zeta,0,0) = alpha A(zeta_0,0,0) + beta A(zeta_inf,0,0) + eta in F; this is proved for generators of vector-field type and open for shift semigroups of multiplicity > 1 and for unbounded skew-adjoint zeta = i m(y) whose [Q, i m] (= -A(zeta,0,0)) lies outside the closure of L.

cards.title: Exact (N,Y,V) chart of F and the tangent problem at the compression
cards.statement: Feasible set: (X,Z) in F iff N := 1 - X X* >= 0 and Y := Z - X Q_BB X* satisfies 0 <= Y <= N. Polar: X = (1-N)^{1/2} V with V : h_B -> h_D the polar partial isometry; V V* = 1 - 1_{{1}}(N), so the POLAR V is a co-isometry iff 1 is not an eigenvalue of N (sharp: for X = the forward shift no co-isometric factor exists); existence of SOME co-isometric factor is the weaker dim ker(1-N) <= dim ker X. Then V* = W U with W the compression unitary h_D -> h_B and U an isometry of h_D (onto iff V unitary). Scaling N = s N_1 (N_1 a bounded positive operator), Y = s Y_1, U_s = 1 + s zeta + o(s) with (U_s) a C_0-semigroup of isometries gives, exactly feasible at every small s, the first-order defect (as sesquilinear forms on C_c^inf) delta^(1) = ddelta + A(zeta,N_1,Y_1) with A_AA = 0, A_AD = -Q_AD zeta + (1/2) Q_AD N_1, A_DD = -(zeta* Q_DD + Q_DD zeta) + (1/2){N_1,Q_DD} - Y_1 (noise enters DD with a MINUS sign); ddelta = [Q,d] with d = E_I D_chi E_I (Lemma 6.1), and ddelta has zero AA block (locality of D_chi, chi = chi' = 0 on A) and zero DD block (Moebius rigidity, S10 Lemma 11.1). Boundary-moving (non-surjective) isometry directions: the absorption identity A(zeta,N_1,Y_1) = A(G, N_1 - 2 sigma, Y_1) holds with G = anti-symmetric part and sigma <= 0 the BOUNDARY FORM <sigma g,g> := Re<zeta* g,g> on dom(zeta*) (sigma <= 0 by Lumer-Phillips for the adjoint contraction semigroup; for BOUNDED zeta, sigma = 0 and zeta is anti-self-adjoint, so bounded isometry families give nothing beyond S10's class). This yields only an INCLUSION of cones (Thm 3.11(3) as amended): its right-hand side consists of the A(G, N_1', Y_1) with G = sigma - zeta* (zeta contained in G + sigma, zeta* = -G + sigma; exact_optimum_tangent_problem.tex:506, :539) the anti-symmetric part of an ADMISSIBLE zeta, N_1' >= 0 a form and 0 <= Y_1 <= N_1', i.e. G is described by how it arises; that G itself generates an isometry semigroup is not claimed (it would need C_c^inf(D) to be a core for zeta, true for zeta_0 and zeta_inf, not assumed in general), and the right-hand side must not be enlarged to all anti-symmetric G. The inclusion cannot be reversed - +lambda D_chi|_D is anti-symmetric but generates an OUTWARD flow, and admitting it would give delta^(1) = (1-lambda) ddelta and tangent value T = 0. Also the singular boundary N_1 are NOT in the g_Q-closure of the bounded ones (||Q_AD N_1^(n)||_2 -> inf), so they need their own one-sided condition, not a limit. The tangent value T = inf g_Q(delta^(1)) is an upper bound for limsup z^{-2} min_F g_Q under hypothesis H1 (g_Q-differentiability along the scaled family); the matching lower bound needs hypothesis H2 (Def 3.16: a minimiser EXISTS, is of the scaled-family form, with ||N_1||+||Y_1|| <= C and a uniform o(s^2) remainder - i.e. H2 is the lower bound in disguise), which is NOT proved: g_Q >= (1/4)||.||_2^2 gives O(s) defect blocks but does not localise (X,Z) because Q_AB has 0 in its essential spectrum.

cards.title: Tangent SDP over (G, N1, Y1) in the circle model: orbit-only optimum matches (1-theta) to 1.1e-7, full optimum not resolvable (measured Gram cond 2.4e22)
cards.statement:
The fixed-geometry tangent problem, min over G = iH anti-Hermitian on D, N1 >= 0, 0 <= Y1 <= N1 of g_Q(delta_c + [G,Q] + noise(N1,Y1)) with noise_DD = (1/2){N1,Q_DD} - Y1, noise_DA = (1/2) N1 Q_DA, noise_AA = 0, was posed as an SDP in the S10 spectral circle model (cvxpy, CLARABEL/SCS). SOLID OUTPUTS. (a) The ORBIT-ONLY restriction (N1 = Y1 = 0 forced) reproduces (1 - theta) g_Q(delta_c) to 1.1e-7 relative at L = 64 (cap 1e10) and 4.0e-7 (cap 1e6) -- this is agreement to 1.1e-7, not "exactly", and it is a statement about the orbit-only problem, i.e. a validation of the SDP formulation against the S10 CG, not about the full tangent optimum. (b) Homogeneity: delta_c -> 2 delta_c scales the ORBIT-ONLY optimum by exactly 4.00000000 in both the direct and the Gram form (L = 64, cap 1e6). (c) The rank-one gains along the KKT-violating directions, computed exactly without a solver, are 6.3e-9, 1.8e-12, 3.5e-11, 1.2e-10, 1.1e-10 in units of g_Q(delta_c) at L = 64, 96, 128, 192, 256 (cap 1e10), and the isometric rotations cannot absorb those directions (g_red/g_Q = 1 - 5e-4); no statement about kappa_opt is made here (that is the business of card kkt-noise-criterion-numerics, in a frame where rigidity is exact). (d) Subspace lower bounds on the gain (f2_sub_gain_fixed.out; each returned (N1,Y1) is checked for cone feasibility, and l and g_red are recomputed exactly outside the solver, so the numbers are valid lower bounds independently of the solver's own objective): at L = 64, subspace eigMtau k=4 gives gain/g_Q(delta_c) = 2.843e-07 (status optimal, cone feasibility -2.4e-12), svdQDA k=4 gives 9.204e-09 (optimal_inaccurate, -4.4e-14), mix k=8 gives 2.106e-04 (optimal_inaccurate, cone feasibility -3.4e-17, l recomputed -1.0000, g_red recomputed 3.2049e+05 by CG; the solver's own objective 6.970e+05 is 2.17x higher, i.e. the returned point is better than the solver thought, and a non-converged CG would only weaken the bound); at L = 128, eigMtau k=4 gives 5.586e-10 (optimal_inaccurate, -7.8e-16). Hence kappa_full <= 1 - theta - 2.106e-4 = 0.64883481 at L = 64 (1 - theta = 0.64904541) and kappa_full <= 0.70882131 at L = 128 (1 - theta = 0.70882131 to 9 digits). The remaining subspaces return no point, with honest solver statuses: infeasible_inaccurate (eigM and rand at L = 64, eigM and mix at L = 128) and infeasible (svdQDA at L = 128).
CORRECTION TO THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS CARD. The earlier statement "at L = 128 and 256 every subspace solve failed" was wrong in its cause: the script crashed with "ValueError: matmul: Input operand 1 does not have enough dimensions" whenever the solver returned no point, because of an unguarded basis @ Nr.value with Nr.value = None. That is a code defect, not conditioning. It has been fixed (status caught, SCS fallback, cone feasibility measured) and the run redone; the table above is the corrected result.
WHAT IS NOT RESOLVED: the FULL tangent optimum kappa_full in the circle model. The quadratic form is numerically singular there: measured Gram condition numbers (f2_gram_cond.out, 3|D|^2 real coordinates) are 2.50e+18 (L = 64, cap 1e4), 2.65e+19 (L = 64, cap 1e6), 2.37e+22 (L = 64, cap 1e10) and 2.51e+26 (L = 96, cap 1e10), with the smallest positive eigenvalue at the double-precision floor -- a direct consequence of the circle model's O(1/L) violation of Moebius rigidity, since the individual blocks of delta_c carry g_Q of order 1e5 x g_Q(delta_c). Consequences observed: CLARABEL fails with SolverError on the direct form at L = 64 for caps 1e4 and 1e10 and on the scale-free cone form for all caps; SCS does not converge in 1e5 iterations; the Gram-reduced form appears to succeed but its answer is a rank-cutoff artefact (it drops 161 of 675 directions below tol*max and then reports kappa_full = 0.5990 against 1 - theta = 0.6490 at L = 64, a spurious 5 percent gain obtained by treating small-curvature directions as free); and the UNCONSTRAINED relaxation (arbitrary Hermitian N1, Y1, no cone) is genuinely ill-posed -- CG on Ghat x = l does not converge and the gain estimate grows monotonically with the iteration count (8.7e-4 -> 6.8e-3 of g_Q(delta_c) between iterations 75 and 200 at L = 64), because with Y1 free the DD block of the defect can be set arbitrarily. The cone constraints are therefore essential and the correct scale-free formulation is q* = min{g_Q([G,Q] + noise(v)) : l(v) = -1, v in the cone} with gain = 1/(4 q*), l(v) = Tr(N1 M_*) - Tr(Y1 tau_*) in the half-SLD normalisation of t_*.
This card reports BOUNDS in the circle model, not a value, and in a frame whose criterion verdict is shown to be artefact-dominated (card kkt-noise-criterion-numerics).

cards.title: Thermal states: two-branch law at the cylinder cross ratio, exponential shielding

cards.title: theta as a geometry-free Wiener-Hopf constant in the modular frame of I
cards.statement: Frame-free form: ddelta = [Q,d] with d = E_I D_chi E_I, and on the isometric orbit delta^(1) = [Q, d - zeta], so 1 - theta = inf_G g_Q([Q, d + G]) / g_Q([Q,d]), the INFIMUM over BOUNDED anti-self-adjoint G supported in D (not a min; the distinction from theta_HS is open, cf. exact_fidelity_upper_half.tex Rem 7.4(i)). In the modular frame of the half-line I = (-inf,1) — coordinate y = -log(1-x), implemented by the half-density push-forward, A = {y<0}, D = {y>0} — Bisognano-Wichmann makes Q a Fourier multiplier Q = (1 + e^{-2 pi p})^{-1}, p = -i d/dy, E_D = 1_{y>0}, and the compression field becomes w(y) = -4 sinh^2(y/2) 1_{y>0} (C^{1,1} at 0, ~ -e^y as y -> +inf: the moving endpoint x=1 sits at y=+inf). With X^ the kernel in the Fourier variable, g_Q([Q,X]) = (1/4) int int K(p,p') |X^(p,p')|^2, K(p,p') = sinh^2(pi(p-p')) / [cosh(pi(p-p')) (cosh(pi(p+p')) + cosh(pi(p-p')))]. So theta is the value of a parameter-free quadratic Wiener-Hopf problem (minimise over kernels supported in the quadrant y,y' > 0): theta is a pure number, independent of a,b,c,L,z. NUMERICAL VALUE (track F3, numerics/optimality_all/F3_RESULTS.md, f3_t0.py): theta = 0.384 +- 0.003, 1 - theta = 0.616 +- 0.003; the modular Galerkin frame and a direct discretisation of the frame above agree to 3e-4 after extrapolation (order h^0.77, five mesh families), the modular window Lambda is irrelevant, and the residual h-dependence is a BULK effect (the endpoint piece saturates at coarse h). S10's 0.300 +- 0.005 is not a competing estimate but a TAPER-SUPPRESSED LOWER BOUND: relaxing the circle model's smoothstep UV taper moves theta at L=256 from 0.2896 to 0.36 and beyond. Consequently the three circulated candidates are EXCLUDED: 3/pi^2 = 0.30396 and 1/3 far below, 1 - 2/pi = 0.36338 still 6.9 sigma low; that all three fell in the old 0.30-0.40 window is a cautionary datum about unmotivated candidates. Structural reading: theta > 0 iff E_D u E_D != 0 (S10 Thm 6.2 + Cor 11.2, non-vanishing numerical). theta < 1 is NOT proved: only the converse is established (if d were anti-self-adjoint then G = -d would be admissible and theta = 1); d is skew-symmetric but not skew-adjoint, its boundary form sitting at the moving endpoint. K -> 1 as |p-p'| -> inf at fixed p+p', and K -> 0 as |p+p'| -> inf at fixed p-p' — the latter is the direction the circle taper suppresses, consistent with its downward bias. NO closed form is claimed or fitted.

cards.title: The first-order gain constant theta = 0.384 +- 0.003 (S10's 0.300 is a taper-suppressed lower bound)
cards.statement: theta = sup_G cos^2(u,v_G) = 0.384 +- 0.003, hence 1-theta = 0.616 +- 0.003. The two published values are reconciled: they are the SAME number at different resolutions, not different limits. Five independent discretisations of F1's geometry-free Wiener-Hopf problem (Prop 6.2) extrapolate to 0.3835-0.3847: T0 uniform cells in the modular coordinate y=-log(1-x) with y_max=10 (theta = 0.31367, 0.34236, 0.35934, 0.36945, 0.37544 at h = 0.24, 0.12, 0.06, 0.03, 0.015) and with y_max=20 (0.31581, 0.34395, 0.36036, 0.37009, 0.37380 at h = 0.24, 0.12, 0.06, 0.03, 0.02); the S11 modular Galerkin frame at a=1, L=2 with Lambda=12 (0.29797 ... 0.36644 at h = 0.32 ... 0.04) and Lambda=8 (0.36608, 0.36962, 0.37346 at h = 0.04, 0.03, 0.02); and the same Galerkin functional on the circle model's own mesh (0.34058, 0.35830, 0.36904, 0.37534, 0.37893 at L = 128...2048). The measured convergence order is h^0.77 +- 0.02 (successive-increment ratio rho = 0.577...0.592 per family -- A: 0.581-0.591, B: 0.581, 0.591, C: 0.577, 0.588, C': 0.592, D: 0.570-0.606 -- stable over four octaves down to h=0.015; fractional because the defect kernel -(i/2pi) sinh(y1/2) sinh(y2/2)/sinh^2((y1-y2)/2) is homogeneous of degree 0 at the corner y=0, confirmed by corner-graded meshes which saturate). The modular-window systematic obeys theta(y_max) = theta_inf - c(h)/y_max with c ~ h^0.6 (residual 1.5e-5), worth +0.0009 to +0.0032. theta is geometry independent: the spread is 5.1e-4 over the four Galerkin rows (a,L) = (1,2), (2,1), (1,4) and s = 0.1, 0.3 at fixed h=0.1, Lambda=12 (0.34843, 0.34894, 0.34854, 0.34863), and 2.0e-3 over the whole table once the T0 (inf,1) row is included (0.34695 at h=0.1, Y=Ymax=8) -- that extra spread is the frame change (T0's smaller modular window, worth about -1.5e-3 by the y_max law above), not the geometry, as Moebius covariance requires. S10 Sec 7(c)'s 0.300 +- 0.005 is a LOWER BOUND: its ultraviolet taper removes the modes carrying ~20% of theta (see finding circle-model-taper-suppresses-theta), and its 1/L Richardson uses the wrong variable (theta_circ rises linearly in log L: 0.28958 -> 0.30173 from L=256 to 1024 with no saturation). Closed forms: 3/pi^2, 1/3, 1-2/pi, (pi^2-6)/12, 2-12/pi^2, 3/8, pi/8 and 16 further candidates are EXCLUDED; 1-pi^2/16 = 0.38315, 2 ln2 - 1 = 0.38629 and 2/pi - 1/4 = 0.38662 lie inside the window; with 26 candidates tested, a window of width 0.006 and 0.28 hits expected by chance, no selection is made (f3_candidates.py / f3_candidates.out). This card SUPERSEDES the window 0.30-0.40 of theta-modular-wiener-hopf / exact_optimum_tangent_problem.tex Sec. 6 (both rewritten 2026-09-15 17:27-17:29 by F1).

cards.title: The theta-problem in the modular frame of the half-line is a parameter-free quadratic Wiener-Hopf problem (F1 Prop. 6.2)
cards.statement: In the modular frame y = -log(1-x) of I = (-inf,1), 1 - theta = inf_G g_Q([Q, d + G]) / g_Q([Q, d]) over bounded anti-self-adjoint G supported in {y > 0}, with d = E_I D_chi E_I and g_Q([Q,X]) = (1/4) int int K(p,p') |X^(p,p')|^2 dp dp', K(p,p') = sinh^2(pi(p-p')) / (cosh(pi(p-p')) [cosh(pi(p+p')) + cosh(pi(p-p'))]), so theta is the value of an explicit quadratic Wiener-Hopf problem independent of the geometry.

cards.title: Theorem A: lim Phi/zeta^2 = c/(12 pi^2)
cards.statement: For the zero-collar geometric compression of the free chiral fermion, Phi(zeta) := -log F(omega, omega^beta) satisfies lim_{zeta->0} Phi/zeta^2 = c/(12 pi^2) = f2 = g_B/8. Lower bound: Legendre form of the SLD metric plus data processing. Upper bound: Uhlmann with a Bogoliubov extension of the compression to a circle diffeomorphism, F >= det(1-V*V)^{1/2}, infimum over extensions = g_B/4 (three-way identity). No interchange of limits or tail bound needed.
cards.verify: Compile rigor/quadratic_limit.pdf (lower) and rigor/uhlmann_upper_bound.pdf (upper); numerics/p1_bogoliubov.out reproduces the bound to 0.2% at zeta = 1/120.

cards.title: Theorem B: f2 = c/(12 pi^2) for every diffeomorphism-covariant net
cards.statement: For every diffeomorphism-covariant net on S^1 (separable, CDIT axioms, Bisognano-Wichmann, Haag duality, Reeh-Schlieder) with (H1) an implementation U_s of the C^{1,1} map, (H2) U_s Omega = Omega + i s T(g_tot) Omega + o(s) with T(g_tot) Omega in the stress-tensor subspace, (H3) first-order differentiability on a core: -log F = (s^2/8) g_B + o(s^2), g_B = 4 dist(T(g_tot) Omega, cl A(I)'_sa Omega)^2 = 2c/(3 pi^2). The stress-tensor subspace reduces Delta and J, c-linearity is structural, the constant comes from the fermion.

cards.title: Two-chirality law for a general 2D CFT (rests on an unproved chiral factorisation)
cards.statement: Conjecture: for a two-dimensional CFT with chiral central charges c = c-bar, the rotated Petz maps of the adjacent-interval configuration give -log F^(lambda) = Phi_c(z(1+e^{-pi lambda})) + Phi_c-bar(z(1+e^{pi lambda})), z = eta_V/(1 - eta_V), with Phi_c the single-chirality zero-collar recovery error of the chiral half (Note 5 eq:collapse-vwz; paper 1 prop:twobranch). The argument uses, without proof, (i) that the net, the vacuum and the rotated Petz map factorise into the two chiral halves, the Bisognano-Wichmann boost acting as t on one light ray and as -t on the other (Note 5 states this in the VWZ paragraph, l. 432-434; paper 1 assumes a tensor-product net A_chiral x A-bar_chiral), and (ii) a per-chirality function Phi_c: the zero-collar collapse (Note 5 cor:collapse) and the normal extension of the glued map behind it are proved only for the free fermion, and for a general chiral net only the second-order coefficient f2 = c/(12 pi^2) is known (Theorem B). Proved special case: the 1+1 massless Dirac fermion (card two-chirality-law).
cards.verify: fidelity_recovered_quasifree.tex sec:rotated, VWZ paragraph and eq:collapse-vwz (l. 426-440); paper1/sec_2d_lattice.tex prop:twobranch and its proof (factorisation over the light-ray coordinates assumed for A_chiral x A-bar_chiral); the proved Dirac case is check_note5_theory.tex prop:chirality <1>1-<1>7.
cards.next: Prove the chiral factorisation of the rotated Petz map for 2D nets of the form A_chiral x A-bar_chiral (and decide the non-tensor-product case), and establish the zero-collar collapse (normal extension of the glued map) for a general chiral net, so that Phi_c is defined.

cards.title: Two-chirality law for the massless Dirac fermion: -log F^(lambda) = Phi(z(1+e^{-pi lambda})) + Phi(z(1+e^{pi lambda})), even in lambda
cards.statement: For the 1+1-dimensional massless Dirac fermion (c = 1: one complex chiral component per chirality), the rotated Petz map of F(O_B) subset F(O_BC) with modular parameter t (lambda = 2t in the convention of Vardhan-Wei-Zou) factorises into the two chiral halves, which act as the geometric maps gamma_{s_t^+-} with s_t^+ = lambda_0 (1 + e^{-2 pi t}) and s_t^- = lambda_0 (1 + e^{+2 pi t}), lambda_0 = c/b the compression parameter of Note 4 (c, b the lengths of C, B); hence -log F^(lambda) = Phi(z(1+e^{-pi lambda})) + Phi(z(1+e^{pi lambda})), with Phi the single-chirality zero-collar recovery error and z = eta_V/(1 - eta_V) (rigor/check_note5_theory.tex prop:chirality <1>1-<1>7). This is even in lambda (interchange of the two arguments; for real lattice states evenness also holds identically by the antiunitary argument, l. 1422-1428), and at lambda = 0 it equals 2 Phi(2z). For a single chirality the rotated family collapses onto one function (Note 5 cor:collapse): -log F(omega, omega-tilde_t) = Phi(z(1 + e^{-2 pi t})), which is nonincreasing in t because Phi is nondecreasing (card phi-monotone-in-zeta); the ordinary Petz map (t = 0) sits at Phi(2z), and Phi(z) <= -log F(omega, omega-tilde_t) for every t: the geometric compression of ABC onto AB (s = lambda_0), the t -> +infinity endpoint, which is a limit point and not a member of the family, is at least as good as every member. Strict monotonicity and continuity of Phi are not proved. NOT claimed here: (i) that the Dirac error is minimal at lambda = 0 for every z (card two-chirality-minimum-at-lambda-zero, conjectural: its only proof step, prop:chirality <1>8, used the false card phi-derivative-nondecreasing); (ii) the law for a general 2D CFT (card two-chirality-law-general-cft, conjectural: it needs a chiral factorisation that is not proved).
cards.verify: rigor/check_note5_theory.tex Prop. 8.2 (prop:chirality, l. 1369-1420), steps <1>1-<1>7 (step <1>8, the minimum, is not claimed); evenness also from the paragraph l. 1422-1428; single chirality: fidelity_recovered_quasifree.tex Cor. 5.1 (cor:collapse, l. 409-420) with check_note5_theory.tex Prop. 8.1 (prop:mono).

cards.title: Two-chirality minimum: for the massless Dirac fermion -log F^(lambda) is minimal at lambda = 0 for every z (unproved)
cards.statement: Conjecture: for the 1+1-dimensional massless Dirac fermion, g(lambda) := Phi(z(1+e^{-pi lambda})) + Phi(z(1+e^{pi lambda})) (the two-chirality law, card two-chirality-law) satisfies g(lambda) >= g(0) = 2 Phi(2z) for every real lambda and every z > 0, i.e. the ordinary Petz map is the best member of the rotated family for two chiralities. No proof exists: the only argument in the documents, rigor/check_note5_theory.tex prop:chirality step <1>8 (l. 1413-1418), uses 'Phi' nondecreasing', which is false (card phi-derivative-nondecreasing, refuted); Note 5 (eq:collapse-vwz) and paper 1 (prop:twobranch) assert the minimum with no valid argument. Known: (a) g is even (card two-chirality-law); (b) for each fixed lambda != 0, g(lambda) > g(0) for all sufficiently small z, since Theorem A gives g(lambda) = f2 z^2 [2 + 4 cosh(pi lambda) + 2 cosh(2 pi lambda)] (1 + o(1)) and the bracket exceeds 8 for lambda != 0 (not uniform in lambda); (c) with t = lambda/2 and zeta_{+-} = z(1 + e^{+-2 pi t}), g'(t) = 2 pi [(zeta_+ - z) Phi'(zeta_+) - (zeta_- - z) Phi'(zeta_-)], so the minimum would follow from the weaker, UNPROVED property that zeta Phi'(zeta) is nondecreasing on (0, infinity) (then (zeta - z) Phi'(zeta) increases on zeta > z); the certified values are consistent with it (zeta Phi' = 5.7e-3, 1.27e-2, 2.11e-2, 3.01e-2, 4.42e-2 at zeta = 1.07, 2.13, 4.27, 8.53, 17.1) and the logarithmic bound that refutes 'Phi' nondecreasing' does not exclude it; (d) on the lattice the small-eta amplitude (-log F^(lambda))/eta^2 = 0.0722, 0.300, 4.49, 70.2 at lambda = 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5 (numerics/lattice/petz_lattice.out [7], eta = 0.0044, n = 64) increases with lambda, and VWZ observe the largest fidelity at lambda = 0.

Values: numerics/kb-checks-2026-09-23/phi_prime_check.out (last column); lattice: petz_lattice.out [7].
cards.next: Prove that zeta Phi'(zeta) is nondecreasing on (0, infinity) (e.g. from the determinant representation, Note 5 Thm 3.1), or bound g(lambda) - g(0) from below with certified values of Phi on a grid plus monotonicity (card phi-monotone-in-zeta); until then the minimum at lambda = 0 is conjectural.

cards.title: (UH) proved: optimised Uhlmann bound = g_Q of the defect, for every isometric quasi-free channel
cards.statement: For an isometric quasi-free channel with one-particle isometry W_I, every unitary W~ of L^2(R) with W~|_{L^2(I)} = W_I and P^perp W~ P Hilbert-Schmidt gives -log F <= -1/2 log det(1 - V^*V) <= -1/2 log(1 - ||V||_2^2), V = P^perp W~ P (Prop. 1.3). The admissible extensions form a right torsor under {1_I (+) W'}: the whole column Z E_I is prescribed by the channel and the free block is E_{I^c} Z E_{I^c}, at first order / as an exact right translation (Lemma 4.1 -- NOT a block-diagonal Z_I (+) Z_e, and NOT the truncation E_I D_chi E_I). Reduction (Thm 4.3): inf over exterior Z_e of (1/2)||P^perp(Z_0+Z_e)P||^2 = (1/2) dist(P^perp Z_0 P, Ext)^2 = (1/2)||Pi P^perp Z_0 P||^2 + (1/2) dist((1-Pi)P^perp Z_0 P, Ext)^2 = g_Q(E_I[P,Z_0]E_I), the last step because closure(Ext) = N^perp always. Hence (UH) in its PROVED, g_Q-free form (Thm 7.1, eq. (18)): for the product family U_s = W~_s e^{-lambda s G} e^{s Z_e}, limsup_{s->0} s^{-2}(-log F(omega, omega^{beta_s})) <= (1/2) dist(P^perp(D_chi + lambda G)P, Ext)^2 = (1/2)||Pi P^perp (D_chi + lambda G) P||^2. Ingredients: the exact one-parameter-group estimate ||P^perp e^{tZ}P||_2 <= |t| ||P^perp Z P||_2 (Lemma 6.1) and an S_2-continuity argument for the three-factor product family (Thm 6.2); the limsup is taken at fixed Z_e and only then the infimum over Z_e (no uniformity in Z_e is claimed or needed). CAVEAT (referee R2): re-expressing the right-hand side as g_Q(delta(s))(1+o(1)) is NOT a consequence of continuity of g_Q (false in the continuum: spec Q accumulates at 0 and 1); it holds whenever S10 Lemma 6.1(2)-(3) applies, with its weight cap (Remark 7.2). Corollary 4.4: the optimised bound depends on the channel only through its first-order defect.

cards.title: Vacuum rigidity: the pulled-back vacuum is the vacuum iff the map is Moebius; no protocol recovers exactly
cards.statement: (a) ELEMENTARY RIGIDITY (Lem 7.1): if Phi: J -> R is C^1 with Phi' > 0 and sqrt(Phi'(x)Phi'(y))/(Phi(x)-Phi(y)) = 1/(x-y) for all x != y in J, then Phi is the restriction of a global Moebius map. Proof: the relation with y = y_1 fixed is the separable ODE g' = g^2/(c (x-y_1)^2) for g = Phi - Phi(y_1), c = Phi'(y_1), whose exact integral (1/g)' = (1/(c(x-y_1)))' gives Phi = Phi(y_1) + c(x-y_1)/(1 + A c (x-y_1)) on each side of y_1; varying the base point and using that two Moebius maps agreeing on an open interval are equal shows the two sides agree. (b) STATE RIGIDITY (Thm 7.3): for the chiral free fermion with vacuum kernel Q(x,y) = (1/2 pi i)(x-y-i0)^{-1}, the state omega o beta_{V_Phi} on F(I) equals the vacuum iff Phi is Moebius iff S(Phi) = 0; the 'only if' follows by testing the two-point function with disjointly supported functions (which avoids the diagonal) and applying (a), the 'if' from [V_g, P] = 0 for g in Moeb (the Moebius group preserves the Hardy space). (c) NO EXACT RECOVERY (Thm 7.3(2,3)): for EVERY non-empty one-sided protocol whose last step keeps a non-empty part, S(Phi) is a non-zero negative measure -- all masses in the general rule -2 sum_m sigma_m G_m'(x_m) delta_{x_m} have the same sign, so they cannot cancel, and the last step's mass is never displaced or swallowed (G_N = id). Hence omega o beta_P != omega and Phi_fid = -log F > 0, using that F = 1 forces equality of the states (Lem 7.2, proved from Alberti's inequality P_tr <= phi(a) psi(a^{-1}) with a = 1 + tb). This needs neither hypothesis (H) nor the second-order law. Degenerate exception: a step conditioning on the ENTIRE block has its corner at an endpoint of I, where beta_I = 0 and zeta = 0; such a step is a pure Moebius compression (Theorem A at a = 0) and is not a recovery in the Petz sense.

cards.title: VWZ four-interval protocols: Phi(1):Phi(2):Phi(3) -> 1:2:4; middle-out is the worst order
cards.statement: In Vardhan-Wei-Zou's symmetric setup (L_A = L_D = a, L_B = L_C = b, their eta (5.9) = a/(a+2b)), the corner calculus (card corner-calculus, open) gives exactly: single step (Protocol 1(A) = 1(B)) one corner of strength zeta_1 = a/b; L->R Protocol 2 corners zeta_2 = a(a+2b)/(2b(a+b)) at p_2 and zeta_3 = a/b at p_3 with e^{Delta_23} = 1/eta; Protocol 3 one double corner of strength 2a/b at p_3 (all checked by REF-P6-0). Hence, given the corner calculus, -log F^(1) : -log F^(3) = Phi_A(a/b) : Phi_A(2a/b) exactly for all eta (-> 1 : 4 as eta -> 0, Theorem A twice, no hypothesis on Ghat), and, CONDITIONAL on the second-order network law with a remainder uniform in the corner separation and on Ghat(Delta) -> 0 as Delta -> inf (both open, corner-correlation-kernel), -log F^(2) -> 2 x -log F^(1); exactly at second order Phi^(2)/Phi^(1) = (zeta_2^2 + zeta_3^2)/zeta_1^2 + (2 zeta_2 zeta_3/zeta_1^2) Ghat(log 1/eta)/Ghat(0). Middle-out is the worst of the three orders at second order with no sign hypothesis: by Cauchy-Schwarz Phi^(2) <= f2 (zeta_2 + zeta_3)^2 < f2 (2 zeta_1)^2 = Phi^(3) because zeta_2 < zeta_1. VWZ (5.10)-(5.11), Fig. 25 state: "-log F^(2) ~ -log F^(3) ∝ f' c eta^2 with f' < f, confirming that the sequential recovery is less effective than the single-step case" -- their inequality and their prose point opposite ways; the calculus contradicts the inequality (f'_3 = 4f exactly) and, at small eta, the approximate equality of Protocols 2 and 3. Their single-step coefficient (2.13), f2 ~ 0.070 c, matches our ordinary-Petz prediction 8 f2 = 0.0675 c (zeta = 2z). Fig. 25 CANNOT be read as a measurement of Ghat (REF-P6-1, rigor/ref_p6_1_fig25.py): Delta_23 = log(1/eta) is bounded below by their axis (eta^2 <= 0.4 gives Delta_23 >= 0.46), the corner strengths there are O(1) (zeta_1 = 2 eta/(1-eta) >= 0.22 for eta >= 0.1) so the second-order law does not apply, and Phi^(2) = Phi^(3) at second order would need Ghat(Delta_23)/Ghat(0) = 1.1 ... 2.1 > 1, which positive-definiteness forbids; no value or sign of Ghat can be extracted from their figure -- G3 measures Ghat directly. Corner measures occurring for four intervals: {p_2} (1(A) = 1(B)), {p_2, p_3} (L->R), {p_3, p_4} (R->L), {2 x p_3} (middle-out); union conditioning regions can move corners off the junctions (corner-calculus).

cards.title: Exact x-space Mellin transform W-hat(k) of the <TT> kernel and its KMS relation
cards.statement: From the stress-tensor two-point function <TT> (card stress-tensor-normalisation, eq:TT) and dilation covariance, the x-space (Mellin) transform of the <TT> kernel is W-hat(k) = (c/(8 pi^2)) int_0^infinity u^{1+ik} (1 - u - i0)^{-4} du = (c/(24 pi)) k (k^2 + 1)/(e^{2 pi k} - 1) for real k != 0, with W-hat(-k) = e^{2 pi k} W-hat(k) (the KMS relation at beta = 2 pi, obtained without a thermal representation) and W-hat >= 0 (rigor/collar_and_invariant_formula.tex prop:What; Beta-function closed form, numerics to 1e-23 in rigor/p4_invariant.py). Numerical check, not a proof about g_B: inserted into Note 7's spectral prescription (analytic continuation of g-hat, eq:barnes) with Note 7's weights, W-hat reassembles the number 2c/(3 pi^2) to relative 1.9e-11 (sec:num); for c = r this coincides with the proved quasi-free integral of quadratic_limit.tex prop:gB (u = 2 pi k). It is not an independent route to the Bures metric: identifying g_B(phi) with this spectral integral is Gap 2 of lemma_second_variation.tex, which the document does not close (sec:collar (b)1, l. 383-392: eq:barnes is 'a prescription, not an identity').

cards.title: S10's circle model: the ultraviolet taper suppresses theta by ~20%, and there is no taper-free limit
cards.statement: Mechanism of the 0.300 vs 0.384 discrepancy. (1) In the NS-circle model of S10 Sec 7 the smoothstep taper on the spectral derivative (window uv in units of L; the Nyquist and the grid's second Fermi point both sit at |nu|/L = 0.5) damps exactly the ultraviolet modes near the moving endpoint where G_* lives. At L=256, a=2, Lg=1: theta = 0.27762, 0.28958, 0.36178, 0.72688, 0.54681 for uv = (0.20,0.32), (0.30,0.42), (0.35,0.47), (0.42,0.49), (0.46,0.499), and 0.17175 with no taper. The sweep is NOT a one-parameter scan: the first three windows share a transition width 0.12, and at that fixed width theta rises monotonically as the taper is relaxed at every L in the file (L=512: 0.28986, 0.29511, 0.32313; L=768: 0.29569, 0.29898, 0.31573); the last two have widths 0.07 and 0.039, and their theta = 0.72688, 0.54681 are artifacts of the sharp transition, not taper-strength data (REF-P0-TAPER). (2) There is NO taper-free limit: without the taper the periodic grid's second Fermi point (nu = +-L/2) doubles the Fermi sea and |u|^2 with it, 0.00739 -> 0.014889 (ratio 2.016), reproducibly in L (0.014889, 0.014912, 0.014921 at L = 256, 512, 768) with theta stuck at 0.17175, 0.19652, 0.20822: the untapered model is STABLE, it simply solves a different problem. Moving the taper's upper edge onto the second Fermi point at fixed transition width does the same (uv = (0.38,0.50): |u|^2 = 0.024005, theta = 0.56798). The |u|^2 = 0.02731 and 0.62691 of the two narrow windows are a separate, transition-sharpness (Gibbs) artifact, NOT the second Fermi point: at the same upper edge with a wider transition the norm is healthy again (uv = (0.25,0.49): 0.007628, theta = 0.36040; uv = (0.09,0.49): 0.007404, theta = 0.30780) (REF-P0-TAPER controls). So the taper is necessary AND it biases theta downwards; S10's window (0.30,0.42) is the safe one and its theta lies below the taper-free value at every L measured; a wider-transition window that passes the same gate more comfortably, uv = (0.25,0.49) (transition width 0.24, |u|^2 3.3% off against the 4.7% for which S10 discards (0.35,0.47)), already gives theta = 0.36040, the taper-free same-mesh value (no superlative is claimed: (0.09,0.49) has a wider transition still and a better norm, 0.007404, but damps the mid-band and gives 0.30780). (3) Proof that the MESH is not responsible (that the taper is the cause is (1)): running the modular Galerkin functional (exact vacuum symbol in closed form, exact continuum defect kernel, no taper, no cap) on the CIRCLE MODEL'S OWN MESH -- cells whose edges are the xi-midpoints of theta_j = 2 pi j / L mapped by xi = log((x+a)/(Lg-x)), x = tan(theta_j/2) -- gives theta = 0.34058, 0.35830, 0.36904, 0.37534, 0.37893 at L = 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, i.e. the Galerkin values, at the same |D| and the same geometry where the tapered circle model gives 0.291, 0.290, 0.295, with |D| = 31, 63, 127, 255 on both sides; and the endpoint cap is not doing the work, since extending it to xi_max = 8.81, 20.81, 260.81 moves theta 0.35830 -> 0.35922 -> 0.35938 -> 0.35938 and saturates (f3_mimic_deep.out). (4) Consequently S10's Richardson in 1/L is also misapplied: the tapered theta_circ rises linearly in log L (theta = 0.28958 -> 0.30173 from L = 256 to 1024; d theta/d log L is flat at 0.0095-0.0096 over L = 512..1024, 0.0094 over 384..1024, and 0.0088 across the quoted endpoints), so continuing that trend to 0.384 would need xi_max ~ 14.8, L ~ 5e6 -- which is a reductio, since a law linear in log L is unbounded and cannot converge to 0.384 at all. S10's proofs P1-P5 and the qualitative conclusions DRAWN FROM theta > 0 ((S) fails, the compression is not the second-order minimiser, E^(2) <= (1-theta) f2 z^2) stand and are strengthened: 1 - theta = 0.616 +- 0.003 instead of 0.70. What does NOT stand is S10's own N2, 'ultraviolet-taper independent', and its verdict box's stability 'in L ... in the ultraviolet taper' (sdp_dual_certificate.tex l.861-863, l.911-913); and N3's non-perturbative 0.705 is a consistency check of the tapered model, not a measurement of 1 - theta.
